- `useChannel<T>(channel: ChannelRef<T> | object, key: string, options?: UseChannelOptions<T>): SubscriptionState<T>` — Receive a createChannel channel's pushes for key. The server authorizes the subscription in this viewer's session (and re-checks it lazily); every publish(key, payload) — from an action, a webhook, a cron — arrives as a new data. At-most-once, latest-wins; no replay on reconnect.
- `interface UseChannelOptions<T>` — Options for useChannel.
- `useLive<A, R>(action: LiveActionRef<A, R>, args: A, options: UseLiveOptions<R>): R | undefined` — Subscribe to a server function's result, re-rendering whenever one of options.tags is invalidated. The function runs on the server under the viewer's own session (it must authorize its own access, like any server action). Pass a **read** action.
- `useLiveOptimistic<T, A>(liveValue: T, reducer: (current: T, action: A) => T): tuple` — Pair an optimistic overlay with a live value: apply a local update immediately, and let it reconcile automatically when the authoritative value arrives over the socket (the overlay resets whenever liveValue's identity changes).
- `interface UseLiveOptions<R>` — Options for useLive.
- `usePresence<S>(room: string, options?: UsePresenceOptions<S>): Presence<S>` — Join a presence room and observe its members (who's-online, cursors, typing…). Orthogonal to cache tags — updates push on join/update/leave.
- `interface UsePresenceOptions<S>` — Options for usePresence.
- `useSubscription<In, Out>(sub: SubscriptionRefLike<In, Out>, input: In, options?: UseSubscriptionOptions<Out>): SubscriptionState<Out>` — Subscribe to a defineSubscription over the Live socket. The server validates input, derives the tags, authorizes on every recompute, and pushes each new value.
- `interface UseSubscriptionOptions<Out>` — Options for useSubscription.

### `denext/lazy`

- `bootResumability(registry: Map<string, unknown>, eager?: boolean, islandsIn?: IslandPayload[], signalStateIn?: Record<string, unknown>): void` — Boot the deferred half of resumability: install delegated qrl dispatch (so serialized data-dnx-h handlers run without hydration), then register every island wrapper for deferred per-island hydration. The generated Flight entry dynamically imports and calls this only when a page carries lazy islands or resumable handlers, so non-resumable apps bundle none of it.

### `denext/desktop`

- `createDesktopHandler(options: RunDesktopOptions, outDir: string, proxy: ProxyModule | undefined, token?: string, onBooted?: () => void | Promise<void>, devProxy?: DesktopProxyFn, devInjectToken?: boolean, bridge?: DesktopBridge, onQuit?: () => void): (request: Request, url: URL) => Promise<Response>` — The desktop request handler: the onRequest escape hatch, the token-gated local endpoints, then — when devProxy is set (denext desktop dev only) — the reverse proxy to denext dev for EVERYTHING else; otherwise the backend proxy, the export's static assets (no-store), the index.html shell for navigations, else 404. Exported for tests; runDesktop wires it to Deno.serve.
- `defineDesktopExtension<C>(capability: C): C` — Define a native desktop extension: a capability that runs in the desktop app's Deno process and that the page calls through denext/desktop/client's desktopExtension. Enable it in desktop.capabilities.extensions (a module path). This is an identity helper — it returns its argument unchanged so a typeof import("./ext.ts") keeps the exact method types the client's typed proxy reads — and it is not a place for side effects (nothing should run at import).
- `DESKTOP_BASELINE_FLAGS: typeOperator` — The permissions every packaged desktop binary needs regardless of capabilities, and which the per-capability flags widen rather than replace: - --allow-net=127.0.0.1,localhost: runDesktop binds loopback and any spa.proxy targets a loopback backend, so the distributed binary can't reach the wider network. - --allow-read (broad): serve the embedded out/ AND the per-user OS app-support directory — a path only known on the end-user's machine, so it can't be baked; the runtime's fs/sqlite caps confine what the page can actually reach. - --allow-env (broad): PORT plus the app's own environment.
- `DESKTOP_DEV_LAN_ENV: DENEXT_DESKTOP_DEV_LAN` — The SECOND dev-only opt-in denext desktop dev --lan sets alongside DESKTOP_DEV_URL_ENV to allow a NON-loopback dev-server target. Without it a non-loopback DENEXT_DESKTOP_DEV_URL is refused at runtime (see desktopDevProxyDecision), so an inherited/hostile env cannot turn a window into a proxy to an arbitrary remote origin.
- `DESKTOP_DEV_URL_ENV: DENEXT_DESKTOP_DEV_URL` — The env var denext desktop dev sets on the deno desktop child to put the runtime into live-reload PROXY mode: its value is the loopback denext dev URL to reverse-proxy to. It is the ONLY switch that turns proxy-all on — a release / run / package invocation never sets it, so those windows serve the static export exactly as before (see runDesktop).
- `interface DesktopBridge` — The runtime bridge: a request handler for its two paths, and an event emitter.
- `desktopBuildFlags(config: unknown, os: DesktopOs): string[]` — The full --allow-* flag list to bake into the deno desktop binary for os — the least-privilege replacement for -A in the package scripts — derived from the WHOLE project config, not just desktop.capabilities (deriving from capabilities alone would starve the non-capability runtime features: an audit found the updater, openAuthSession and a non-loopback proxy all broke). On top of DESKTOP_BASELINE_FLAGS it adds: - the enabled capabilities' run / ffi / sys exactly (the real least-privilege wins), and a single broad --allow-write when any capability writes (a per-user path can't be baked; the runtime cap layer confines it); - a non-loopback spa.proxy target's host, MERGED into the single --allow-net (Deno keeps only the last --allow-net, so every host is one flag); - desktop.extraPermissions — the escape hatch for what the catalog can't see: the updater's feed host (net) and data dir (write), an extension's own run/ffi, etc. It is UNIONED in, and --regenerate-scripts preserves it because it lives in the config, not the script. A capability's read/env is dropped (already broad in the baseline); a capability's net (only downloadToFile's *) is dropped too — per-host download access is an extraPermissions grant, never * baked in.
- `interface DesktopCapability` — A desktop capability: a name (its address on the bridge — an extension's name is its cap name), a set of methods, and the event names it may DesktopCapCtx.emit. Built-ins live in ./caps; user extensions are authored with defineDesktopExtension.
- `interface DesktopCapabilityMethod<I, O>` — One capability method: an optional input schema (validated before the handler), an optional output schema (strips the result before it reaches the page, in production too), the Deno permissions it needs, an optional per-method timeout, and the handler that runs in the Deno process.
- `interface DesktopCapCtx` — The context a capability handler runs with: a scoped DesktopCapCtx.emit for its declared events, the OS app-support directory (which survives relaunch, unlike browser storage — see the desktop storage note), the running OS, the app window (Deno's BrowserWindow when the runtime exposes it), and an AbortSignal that fires when the handler's timeout elapses.
- `class DesktopCapError` — Throw this from a capability handler to answer the page with a specific error code and a SAFE message. The bridge puts code, the message and any data into the { ok: false, error } envelope at status (default 400). Never encode an absolute path, environment value or stack into the message — it crosses to the page. The code "unavailable" is RESERVED (it means the capability/method is not enabled, which makes the page fall back to its web path); use another code for a real failure.
- `desktopDevProxyDecision(devUrl: string | undefined, lan: boolean, execPath: string): DesktopDevProxyDecision` — Decide whether runDesktop enters live-reload PROXY mode, enforcing the loopback rule at RUNTIME rather than trusting the env (invariant: a release build never proxies to a remote origin). Pure + testable. Proxy mode requires ALL of: - a devUrl (the DESKTOP_DEV_URL_ENV value); - execPath being the deno CLI (isDenoCliExecPath) — a packaged app IGNORES the env, so an inherited/hostile env cannot turn a shipped window into a proxy; - a parseable URL whose host is loopback — OR non-loopback WITH lan (the DESKTOP_DEV_LAN_ENV opt-in that only desktop dev --lan sets). allowNonLoopback is true only in that LAN case. A blocked case returns { proxy: false, refused } so the caller can log why and serve static.
- `type DesktopDevProxyDecision = object | object` — The live-reload proxy decision from the env + the running binary — see desktopDevProxyDecision.
- `class DesktopEventLog` — A bounded, replayable log of desktop bridge events. One instance per running app (created by the bridge); exported as a type so DesktopBridge["events"] is documentable.
- `desktopIncludeArgs(entryUrl: string): Promise<string[]>` — The extra --include <path> args a scaffolded packaging script must add so the packaged binary embeds each desktop.capabilities.extensions module — otherwise the app launches but the runtime fails to load the extension ("Module not found"), since --include out only bundles the export. Reads the project's denext.config.ts next to entryUrl (a scripts/ script → ../), like desktopPackageFlags; a project with no extensions gets [].
- `type DesktopOs = darwin | windows | linux` — The operating systems a Deno Desktop app ships for (Deno.build.os spelling).
- `desktopPackageFlags(entryUrl: string, os: DesktopOs): Promise<string[]>` — The deno desktop --allow-* flags for a scaffolded packaging script: read the project's denext.config.ts (next to entryUrl — a packaging script lives in scripts/, so the config is ../denext.config.ts) and derive the least-privilege flags for os via desktopBuildFlags. A project without a config (or one that exports none) gets the baseline. The config is imported dynamically at run time from a caller-supplied URL, so it is never part of this module's own dependency graph (nor a build-time import of user code).
- `interface DesktopPermissions` — The Deno permissions a capability method needs, as --allow-* scopes. The union of every enabled capability's descriptor is what the package scripts bake into the desktop binary instead of -A (least-privilege packaging), and what denext doctor reports. An ffi or run entry means full-trust native code: least-privilege is moot for that surface once it is on.
- `type DesktopProxyFn = (request: Request, url: URL) => Response | Promise<Response>` — Forward a request the desktop window received to the denext dev server. Injected into createDesktopHandler so tests exercise the dev path with a spy and never spawn a real dev server; runDesktop wires it to proxyToBackend.
- `injectDesktopGlobal(html: string, token: string | null, beacon?: boolean): Promise<string>` — Inject globalThis.__denext = { desktop: true, token } as an inline <script> immediately after the opening <head> (falling back to after <body>, then to a prepend). The value is JSON.stringify-escaped. When beacon is set, the boot-confirm beacon (BOOT_BEACON_JS) is appended to the SAME script so one CSP hash covers both. When the shell carries a hash-based CSP meta, its script-src is extended with this script's 'sha256-…' so the script survives a strict policy.
- `isDenoCliExecPath(execPath: string): boolean` — Whether execPath is the deno CLI (deno / deno.exe, case-insensitive) rather than a compiled/packaged app binary. Live-reload proxy mode runs under deno desktop <entry>, so its execPath is deno; a packaged app's is its own binary. Pure, so the packaged-vs-dev decision is testable without the real Deno.execPath.
- `type ProxyModule = ./dev-proxy.ts` — The lazily-imported reverse-proxy module (./dev-proxy.ts) createDesktopHandler forwards to when a backend proxy is configured; exported so the handler's signature is public.
- `interface ResolvedDesktop` — What resolveDesktopCapabilities returns — spread straight into runDesktop.
- `resolveDesktopCapabilities(config: DenextConfig | undefined, options?: ResolveDesktopOptions): Promise<ResolvedDesktop>` — Resolve config.desktop.capabilities into the capability objects the bridge serves, plus the app-support directory the runtime hands to handlers.
- `interface ResolveDesktopOptions` — Options for resolveDesktopCapabilities.
- `resolveOutDir(options: RunDesktopOptions): string` — The static-export dir to serve: outDir (relative to importMetaUrl when given), else out/.
- `runDesktop(options?: RunDesktopOptions): Promise<void>` — Serve a denext SPA export in a deno desktop window. Adopts the initial Deno.BrowserWindow and quits the process on window close; under a plain deno run (no desktop runtime) it just starts the server.
- `interface RunDesktopOptions` — Options for runDesktop (and createDesktopHandler): where to serve the static export from, an optional loopback reverse proxy and request escape hatch, the signed self-updater, the enabled capability bridge, the app-support directory, and whether the loopback OAuth endpoint is enabled. The generated desktop.ts entry spreads resolveDesktopCapabilities into it.
- `stripDesktopCredentials(request: Request): Request` — The request to forward to the dev server with the desktop credential removed: the per-launch x-denext-desktop-token header is dropped so it never reaches the dev server (invariant: the token gates the LOCAL endpoints only). A WebSocket upgrade is returned untouched — it cannot be reconstructed (Deno.upgradeWebSocket needs the original connection), a browser cannot set a custom header on a WS handshake, and proxyToBackend's WS bridge forwards only host/origin/cookie upstream, never the token. denext injects no desktop-specific cookie (the token lives in globalThis.__denext and this header only), so there is none to strip.

### `denext/desktop/updater`

- `applyDesktopUpdate(version: string, config: DesktopUpdaterConfig): Promise<void>` — Promote the staged version to the active overlay and flip the "current" pointer atomically. Re-verifies the staged manifest (version + signature) and re-hashes every staged file BEFORE the swap. The previous version dir is kept for rollback, the accepted sequence is recorded, and the new version starts PENDING — desktopBooted must confirm it or the next resolveDesktopUiDir rolls it back.
- `checkForDesktopUpdate(config: DesktopUpdaterConfig): Promise<DesktopUpdateCheck>` — Check the feed for a newer, fully-verified UI. Fetches ${feedUrl}/_denext/ota.json, validates its shape, RECOMPUTES the version and refuses a mismatch, VERIFIES the ECDSA signature, and refuses a non-monotonic sequence — all BEFORE reporting anything as available. A version equal to the active overlay resolves { available: false }.
- `desktopBooted(config: DesktopUpdaterConfig): Promise<void>` — Confirm that the active overlay booted. Call it once the app has served and rendered (the desktop runtime calls it behind a short delay after Deno.serve is up). It flips a PENDING pointer to confirmed and clears the watchdog marker, so a crash BEFORE this call leaves the version pending and the next resolveDesktopUiDir rolls it back. Best effort: it never throws.
- `interface DesktopUpdateCheck` — The result of checkForDesktopUpdate.
- `class DesktopUpdateError` — A refusal from the updater, carrying a machine-readable DesktopUpdateErrorCode.
- `type DesktopUpdateErrorCode = network | invalid | integrity | unsigned | signature | downgrade | not_staged | rejected` — The code on a DesktopUpdateError:
- `interface DesktopUpdatePrepared` — The result of prepareDesktopUpdate.
- `interface DesktopUpdaterConfig` — Configuration for the desktop UI self-updater.
- `desktopUpdateReset(config: DesktopUpdaterConfig): Promise<void>` — Return to the bundled export: delete every overlay version, every staging dir, and all state (pointer, sequence, rejected, marker). A no-op when nothing is installed.
- `desktopUpdateStatus(config: DesktopUpdaterConfig): Promise<DesktopUpdateStatus>` — A snapshot of the overlay state (mirrors otaStatus).
- `interface DesktopUpdateStatus` — A snapshot of the overlay state, mirroring OtaStatus on mobile.
- `interface OtaManifest` — The _denext/ota.json document: a version stamped over the sorted file list.
- `interface OtaManifestFile` — One file of an OTA UI.
- `prepareDesktopUpdate(config: DesktopUpdaterConfig): Promise<DesktopUpdatePrepared>` — Download and verify a newer UI into a STAGING directory WITHOUT switching to it. Files whose SHA-256 already matches the active overlay are copied (reused) instead of re-downloaded; every staged file is then re-hashed and refused if it does not match its manifest entry. The manifest version and signature are re-verified. Any failure discards the staging dir — nothing is ever partially applied. Switch with applyDesktopUpdate.
- `resolveDesktopUiDir(bundledOut: string, config: DesktopUpdaterConfig): Promise<string>` — The directory the desktop runtime should serve: the active verified overlay, or bundledOut.

### `denext/desktop/client`

- `interface DesktopBridgeError` — A failed desktop bridge call. Narrow with isDesktopBridgeError.
- `type DesktopErrorCode = unavailable | forbidden | validation | timeout | too_large | bridge_error | parenthesized` — Why a desktop call failed:
- `desktopExtension<M>(name: string): DesktopExtensionClient<M>` — A typed client for the desktop extension name. Each property is an async function that calls that method in the Deno process through the bridge.
- `type DesktopExtensionClient<M> = conditional` — The typed proxy desktopExtension returns: one async function per method.
- `type DesktopExtensionModule = object | object` — An extension (or the module that default-exports it) as the typing reads it.
- `type DesktopExtensionOf<M> = conditional` — The extension itself: the module's default export, or the value given.
- `type DesktopMethodInput<Mth> = conditional` — What the page passes to a method: its input schema's input type, else the handler's argument.
- `type DesktopMethodOutput<Mth> = conditional` — What a method resolves on the page: its output schema's output type, else the handler's result.
- `interface DesktopMethodShape` — One extension method as the typing reads it: an input schema, an output schema, a handler.
- `interface DesktopRpcOptions` — Options for desktopRpc.
- `interface DesktopSchemaTypes<In, Out>` — The slice of a Standard Schema (https://standardschema.dev) the extension typing reads: its input and output types.
- `isDesktopBridgeError(value: unknown): value is DesktopBridgeError` — Whether value is a DesktopBridgeError.
- `onDesktopEvent<T>(cap: string, event: string, handler: (data: T) => void): () => void` — Call handler for each event the desktop runtime emits for cap: an extension's name (its handlers emit the events it declares with ctx.emit), or a built-in capability that emits events (today only the echo diagnostic's pong). The first subscription opens the event stream and the last unsubscribe closes it; frames that arrived before a handler for that event subscribed are delivered to it once it does. Off desktop it does nothing.

### `denext/mobile`

- `type AppFileDirectory = documents | data | cache` — The app's own folders:
- `interface AppleSignInOptions` — Options for signInWithApple.
- `applyFontScale(options?: ApplyFontScaleOptions): () => void` — Opt in to the OS text size: scale the root element's font size (as the page's stylesheet sets it when this is called) by getFontScale's factor, so everything sized in rem / em follows Dynamic Type (iOS) and the font scale (Android), and keep it current. The factor is also set as the --dnx-font-scale custom property, for sizes the page computes itself (calc(15px * var(--dnx-font-scale))). A browser's own text-size setting already reaches rem, so on the web this sets nothing but the property (1).
- `interface ApplyFontScaleOptions` — Options for applyFontScale.
- `applyUiUpdate(version: string): Promise<OtaApplyResult>` — Switch to the UI prepareUiUpdate staged: the native side starts its trial, arms the rollback watchdog (15 s of foreground time by default), points the webview at it and reloads. The new page must call otaBooted, exactly as after checkForUiUpdate.
- `interface AppStoreOptions` — Where openAppStore sends the user.
- `type AppUpdateAvailability = unknown | not-available | available | in-progress | unsupported` — Whether the store has a newer build: the plugin's AppUpdateAvailability, named.
- `interface AppUpdateInfo` — What getAppUpdateInfo reports. Fields a platform does not know are absent.
- `type AppUpdateOutcome = accepted | cancelled | failed | not-available | not-allowed | info-missing | unsupported` — How an in-app update call ended: the plugin's AppUpdateResultCode, named, plus "unsupported" (not Android, or no plugin).
- `attachContextMenu(el: ContextMenuElement, items: ContextMenuItems, onSelect: (id: string) => void, options?: ContextMenuTargetOptions): () => void` — Bind a context menu to el: a long press (or a right click) opens it and onSelect gets the chosen item's id. Inside the iOS shell with denext mobile add context-menu it is the system's UIContextMenuInteraction with the lifted element as its preview; see the module docs for the other platforms.
- `authenticateBiometric(options?: BiometricAuthOptions): Promise<void>` — Ask the user to authenticate with Face ID / Touch ID / a fingerprint (or, with allowDeviceCredential, the device passcode).
- `interface AuthSessionError` — The Error an openAuthSession promise rejects with.
- `type AuthSessionErrorCode = cancelled | busy | invalid | unsupported | timeout` — The code on an openAuthSession rejection:
- `interface AuthSessionOptions` — Options for openAuthSession.
- `interface AuthSessionResult` — What openAuthSession resolves with.
- `type BackEdge = left | right | none` — Which screen edge a back gesture started from ("none": a button, or unknown).
- `interface BackGesture` — A back gesture in flight, as useBackProgress reports it.
- `interface BackgroundKeyValue` — The key/value store a task sees: UserDefaults on iOS, SharedPreferences on Android.
- `interface BackgroundLocationOptions` — Options for watchPositionInBackground.
- `interface BackgroundTask` — A task, as defineBackgroundTask returns it (the module's default export).
- `interface BackgroundTaskContext` — What a task's handler receives.
- `interface BackgroundTaskDefinition` — The input to defineBackgroundTask.
- `type BackHandler = () => boolean | void` — A back handler: return true to consume the back action (nothing below it runs, the app stays where it is); anything else passes it to the handler registered before it, and after the last one to the default (history back, else leave the app).
- `type BackProgressEvent = object | object` — One predictive-back event: the gesture starts and makes progress, then is cancelled (the user let go short of the threshold) or committed (the back action runs next).
- `interface BackSwipeOptions` — Options for useBackSwipe and isBackSwipe.
- `type BarcodeFormat = qr_code | aztec | codabar | code_39 | code_93 | code_128 | data_matrix | ean_13 | ean_8 | itf | pdf417 | upc_a | upc_e` — A barcode format, by its BarcodeDetector name.
- `interface BarcodeScanError` — The Error a scanBarcode promise rejects with for the codes above.
- `type BarcodeScanErrorCode = unsupported | denied` — The code on a scanBarcode rejection: unsupported (no scanner here: no plugin, and no BarcodeDetector or camera in the browser, or none of the formats asked for) or denied (camera permission refused).
- `interface BiometricAuthOptions` — Options for authenticateBiometric.
- `interface BiometricAvailability` — What the device offers, from isBiometricAvailable.
- `interface BiometricError` — A failed authenticateBiometric (or a biometric-gated secureStore.get).
- `type BiometricErrorCode = cancelled | fallback | lockout | not-enrolled | unavailable | passcode-not-set | failed | unsupported` — Why a biometric check failed, as BiometricError's code reports it.
- `type BiometricType = face | fingerprint | iris` — A kind of biometric sensor.
- `interface CalendarComponents` — The date components a calendar trigger matches.
- `cancelAllNotifications(): Promise<void>` — Cancel every pending local notification. Outside the shell it does nothing.
- `cancelNotification(ids: number | typeOperator): Promise<void>` — Cancel pending local notifications (and remove delivered ones with those ids on Android). An id that is not pending is ignored. Outside the shell it does nothing.
- `checkForUiUpdate(options: OtaCheckOptions): Promise<OtaCheckResult>` — Check a server for a newer UI and, when it offers a different version, install it.
- `checkPermission(name: PermissionName): Promise<PermissionState>` — The current status of a permission, without prompting (see PermissionState for what each status means).
- `completeAuthSession(): boolean` — Finish a web openAuthSession: call it on the callback page the provider redirects the popup to (an https page of the same origin). It posts this page's full URL (code, state and all) to the window that opened the popup, addressed to this origin only, then closes the popup. Not needed inside the native shell, where the callback never loads a page.
- `completeFlexibleUpdate(): Promise<void>` — Android: install a downloaded flexible update, restarting the app. A no-op elsewhere.
- `configurePurchases(config: PurchasesConfig): Promise<void>` — Configure RevenueCat once, early (a root layout's effect), before any other purchases call.
- `interface ContextMenuElement` — The slice of an element a bound menu uses (real DOM and the test DOM both satisfy it).
- `interface ContextMenuItem` — One entry in a showContextMenu menu.
- `type ContextMenuItems = typeOperator | parenthesized` — The items of a bound menu, or a function that builds them when the menu opens.
- `interface ContextMenuOptions` — Where and how showContextMenu opens.
- `interface ContextMenuTargetOptions` — Options for useContextMenu and attachContextMenu.
- `interface CrashReportingOptions` — Options for initCrashReporting.
- `interface CrashReportingStarted` — What initCrashReporting started with.
- `createAlbum(name: string): Promise<MediaAlbum>` — Create an album (a no-op when one with that name exists).
- `createNotificationChannel(channel: NotificationChannel): Promise<void>` — Create (or update the name / description of) an Android notification channel. A notification's channelId picks it; Android 8+ requires one (the plugin creates a default). Resolves without doing anything on iOS and the web, which have no channels.
- `interface CustomerInfo` — What the user is entitled to (RevenueCat's CustomerInfo).
- `interface DeepLinkEvent` — One link that opened the app.
- `interface DeepLinkOptions` — Options for onDeepLink and useDeepLink.
- `defineBackgroundTask(definition: BackgroundTaskDefinition): BackgroundTask` — Declare a background task: the default export of a background/<name>.ts module.
- `deleteFile(path: string, options?: FileLocationOptions): Promise<void>` — Delete a file.
- `deleteNotificationChannel(id: string): Promise<void>` — Delete an Android notification channel (nothing elsewhere).
- `deleteSqlite(name: string, options?: SqliteOptions): Promise<void>` — Delete the database name (closing it first when open). A missing database is not an error.
- `deviceInfo(): Promise<DeviceInfo>` — Facts about the device the page runs on.
- `interface DeviceInfo` — What deviceInfo reports. Only platform is always known.
- `downloadToFile(url: string, path: string, options?: FileLocationOptions): Promise<object>` — Download a URL straight into a file (missing parent folders are created).
- `endLiveActivity(id: string, options?: EndLiveActivityOptions): Promise<void>` — End a Live Activity.
- `interface EndLiveActivityOptions` — Options for endLiveActivity.
- `interface EntitlementInfo` — One entitlement's state.
- `interface EntitlementState` — What useEntitlement returns.
- `type FileDirectory = AppFileDirectory | PickedDirectory` — Where a file lives: one of the app's own folders (AppFileDirectory), or a file or folder the user picked (PickedDirectory).
- `type FileEncoding = utf8 | base64` — How text is carried: "utf8" (plain text, the default) or "base64" (binary data).
- `interface FileEntry` — One entry of a listDir listing.
- `interface FileLocationOptions` — Options for deleteFile, listDir and downloadToFile.
- `interface FlexibleUpdateProgress` — A flexible update's progress, from onFlexibleUpdateProgress.
- `interface GeolocationError` — A failed location read.
- `type GeolocationErrorCode = denied | unavailable | timeout | unsupported` — Why a location read failed, as GeolocationError's code reports it.
- `interface GeoPosition` — A position fix.
- `interface GeoPositionOptions` — How precise, fresh and quick a fix should be.
- `getAlbums(): Promise<MediaAlbum[]>` — The albums of the photo library the app can see: on iOS every album (after the user grants full access), on Android the albums this app created (the plugin's default, non-gallery mode).
- `getAppUpdateInfo(options?: object): Promise<AppUpdateInfo>` — Ask the store whether a newer build of the app exists.
- `getCurrentPosition(options?: GeoPositionOptions): Promise<GeoPosition>` — One position fix.
- `getCustomerInfo(): Promise<CustomerInfo>` — What the user is entitled to now (RevenueCat caches it; it refreshes in the background).
- `getFontScale(): Promise<number>` — The OS text size as the factor the page must still apply itself: 1 at the default size.
- `getOfferings(): Promise<PurchaseOfferings>` — The offerings configured in the RevenueCat dashboard, with the store's localized prices.
- `getOrientation(): Promise<Orientation>` — Read the screen's orientation.
- `getRecentMedia(options?: RecentMediaOptions): Promise<MediaItem[]>` — The newest photos and videos in the library, with thumbnails (iOS only: Android's plugin has no media query, and the web has no library).
- `getTrackingStatus(): Promise<TrackingStatus>` — Read the ATT status without prompting.
- `interface GoogleSignInOptions` — Options for signInWithGoogle.
- `haptic(kind: HapticKind): Promise<void>` — Play a short haptic.
- `type HapticKind = light | medium | heavy | success | warning | error | selection` — A haptic feedback kind haptic can play.
- `hideKeyboard(): Promise<void>` — Dismiss the on-screen keyboard: Keyboard.hide() in the native shell with @capacitor/keyboard, else by blurring the focused element (which closes the keyboard in mobile browsers). Does nothing during SSR.
- `hideSplash(): Promise<void>` — Hide the native launch splash screen, through @capacitor/splash-screen inside the shell (denext mobile add splash). Call it once the first screen has rendered, when the plugin is configured with launchAutoHide: false. On the web, and when the plugin is not installed, it does nothing.
- `interface IdTokenSession<User>` — The session half signInNative drives: nativeSession(...) from denext.
- `type ImageSource = camera | photos | prompt` — Where pickImage gets the picture: "camera" (take one), "photos" (the photo library) or "prompt" (ask the user which; the default).
- `initCrashReporting(opts: CrashReportingOptions): Promise<CrashReportingStarted>` — Start crash reporting once: load the SDKs, work out the release (the OTA UI version), and call Sentry.init(options, sibling.init). Later calls return the first call's result. Call it as early as possible, before the app renders.
- `installKeyboardInset(opts?: KeyboardInsetOptions): () => void` — Keep a CSS custom property on document.documentElement (default --denext-keyboard-inset) equal to the on-screen keyboard's height in px, so layout can lift a composer or a bottom bar above it: padding-bottom: var(--denext-keyboard-inset).
- `installMomentumSafeScroll(options?: MomentumSafeScrollOptions): () => void` — Keep iOS momentum scrolling alive while scroll-anchoring code corrects the scroll offset.
- `installOfflineScreen(opts?: OfflineScreenOptions): () => void` — Show a full-screen offline notice whenever the device loses its connection. Idempotent per page: a second call replaces the first. A no-op without a DOM (SSR, workers).
- `isBackgroundLocationAvailable(): boolean` — Whether background location is available here: the shell has the BackgroundGeolocation plugin (denext mobile add background-location). When false, watchPositionInBackground watches in the foreground only.
- `isBackSwipe(dx: number, dy: number, opts?: BackSwipeOptions): boolean` — The pure gesture test behind useBackSwipe: whether a movement of dx/dy CSS px from the touch start is a back swipe, i.e. rightward by at least minDistance and horizontal by at least ratio × the absolute vertical movement.
- `isBiometricAvailable(): Promise<BiometricAvailability>` — Whether biometric authentication can succeed on this device now, and which sensor it uses.
- `isNativeShell(): boolean` — Whether the page runs inside a Capacitor iOS/Android native shell (webview origin capacitor://localhost on iOS, https://localhost on Android). false on the web, when @capacitor/core is merely bundled into a web build, and during SSR.
- `isScreenReaderEnabled(): Promise<boolean>` — Whether a screen reader is on: VoiceOver on iOS, a touch-exploration service (TalkBack) on Android, through the DenextAccessibility plugin that denext mobile add accessibility installs. On the web, during SSR, in a shell without the plugin, or when the plugin fails, it resolves false.
- `type KeyboardAvoidingBehavior = padding | height | position` — How a KeyboardAvoidingView makes room: add bottom padding, shrink its height, or move up as a whole (a compositor-only translateY).
- `KeyboardAvoidingView(props: KeyboardAvoidingViewProps): VNode` — A <div> that makes room for the on-screen keyboard, like React Native's KeyboardAvoidingView: with behavior="padding" (the default) it adds the covered height to its bottom padding, with "height" it shrinks its height by it (from style.height, else 100%), and with "position" it moves up by it. keyboardVerticalOffset subtracts a fixed amount (a bottom bar the keyboard hides anyway).
- `interface KeyboardAvoidingViewProps` — Props of KeyboardAvoidingView; any other prop goes to its <div>.
- `interface KeyboardInsetOptions` — Options for installKeyboardInset and useKeyboardInset.
- `type KeyboardResizeMode = native | body | ionic | none` — How @capacitor/keyboard resizes the app when the keyboard shows (iOS only): the whole WebView ("native", the plugin's default), only <body>, only ion-app, or nothing ("none": the keyboard covers the page, and KeyboardAvoidingView lifts it).
- `interface KeyboardState` — The keyboard as useKeyboard and onKeyboardChange report it.
- `KeyboardStickyView(props: KeyboardStickyViewProps): VNode` — A <div> that rides on top of the on-screen keyboard: while the keyboard covers the page it moves up by the covered height (a compositor-only translateY), and back down when the keyboard hides. Place it at the bottom of the screen yourself (position: fixed / sticky, bottom: 0); the view only adds the transform. This is the composer of a chat screen: see the chat-composer recipe on /docs/mobile.
- `interface KeyboardStickyViewProps` — Props of KeyboardStickyView; any other prop goes to its <div>.
- `type KeyboardViewStyle = Readonly<Record<string, string | number | undefined>>` — An inline style object, as the views accept and extend it.
- `type KeyValueBackend = native | sqlite | desktop | indexeddb | memory` — Where a KeyValueStore keeps its data: "native" (the DenextStorage plugin), "sqlite" (@capacitor-community/sqlite in the shell), "desktop" (the Deno Desktop runtime's SQLite), "indexeddb" (the browser's; evictable inside a native shell) or "memory" (gone when the page closes).
- `interface KeyValueStore` — A named, durable string store (openKeyValueStore).
- `type LinkAccept = parenthesized | LinkAllowList` — Which incoming links to act on: a predicate over the parsed URL, or an allow-list.
- `interface LinkAllowList` — An allow-list for incoming links.
- `type LinkRoute = boolean | parenthesized` — How to navigate to an accepted link: true navigates with the page's router, false leaves it to the callback, and a function navigates itself (e.g. (path) => router.push(path)).
- `listDir(path: string, options?: FileLocationOptions): Promise<FileEntry[]>` — List a folder's entries.
- `listLiveActivities(): Promise<RunningLiveActivity[]>` — The running Live Activities of the app (started here, earlier, or by a push-to-start push).
- `listNotificationChannels(): Promise<NotificationChannel[]>` — The app's Android notification channels (none elsewhere).
- `interface LiveActivityError` — The Error a Live Activity function rejects with.
- `type LiveActivityErrorCode = unsupported | disabled | invalid | not_found | timeout | failed` — The code on a Live Activity rejection:
- `liveActivityPushToken(id: string, options?: LiveActivityTokenOptions): Promise<string>` — The ActivityKit push token of a Live Activity started with { push: true }, as hex, for a server to update it through APNs (apns-push-type: liveactivity, with a content-state in the shape of the state object). It waits for the token when ActivityKit has not issued it yet.
- `interface LiveActivityPushTokenEvent` — A push token ActivityKit issued a running Live Activity.
- `liveActivityPushToStartToken(options?: LiveActivityTokenOptions): Promise<LiveActivityPushToStartToken | null>` — The app's ActivityKit push-to-start token (iOS 17.2 and later), as hex: a server sends it an APNs push (apns-push-type: liveactivity, "event": "start", "attributes-type": "DenextActivityAttributes", "attributes": { "name": <Live Activity name>, "values": { … } } and a content-state in the shape of the state object) to start a Live Activity while the app is not running. It waits for the token when ActivityKit has not issued it yet; onLiveActivityPushToStartToken reports later ones. The app needs the push entitlement (denext mobile add push), without which no token comes (timeout).
- `interface LiveActivityPushToStartToken` — A push-to-start token ActivityKit issued the app (iOS 17.2+).
- `interface LiveActivityTokenOptions` — Options for liveActivityPushToken and liveActivityPushToStartToken.
- `type LiveActivityValues = Readonly<Record<string, unknown>>` — A JSON object: a Live Activity's attributes or state.
- `interface LocalNotification` — A local notification as the received / tapped events report it.
- `interface LocalNotificationInput` — A local notification to schedule.
- `interface LocalNotificationTap` — A tap on (or an action of) a local notification.
- `type LocalNotificationTapOptions = PushTapOptions` — Options for onLocalNotificationTapped: the same link rules as a push tap.
- `type LocalNotificationTrigger = object | object | object | object | object | object | parenthesized` — When a local notification fires. Months are 1–12 and weekdays 1–7 with 1 = Sunday (the plugin's and iOS's convention); times are the device's local time.
- `interface LocationState` — What useLocation returns.
- `lockOrientation(orientation: OrientationLock): Promise<void>` — Lock the screen to an orientation (a video player going landscape, a scanner staying portrait). Undo it with unlockOrientation.
- `materialNameFor(sfName: string): string | undefined` — The Material Symbol an SF Symbol name maps to: the .fill suffix becomes the -fill variant (when there is one), and trailing components are dropped until a stem is known (heart.circle.fill → favorite-fill).
- `interface MediaAlbum` — An album, as getAlbums lists it.
- `interface MediaItem` — One item from getRecentMedia.
- `interface MomentumSafeScrollOptions` — Options for installMomentumSafeScroll and useMomentumSafeScroll (denext/mobile).
- `moveToTrash(item: ShellItem): Promise<void>` — Move a file or folder to the Trash (macOS), Recycle Bin (Windows) or the freedesktop trash (Linux), so the user can restore it.
- `type NativeCallConvention = options | positional` — How a call's arguments reach the native method and how its result comes back.
- `type NativeMethod<F> = conditional` — A native method's typed client: the same arguments, and the result as a Promise.
- `nativeModule<T, E>(name: string, options?: NativeModuleOptions): NativeModuleClient<T, E> | null` — A typed client for your own native plugin name: the Capacitor plugin of that name inside the iOS/Android shell, the desktop extension of that name in a Deno Desktop window, else null (on the web, during SSR, or when the shell has no such plugin).
- `type NativeModuleClient<T, E> = NativeModuleMethods<T> & NativeModuleEvents<E>` — What nativeModule returns: T's methods (async) plus addListener.
- `interface NativeModuleEvents<E>` — The event half of a NativeModuleClient: payloads typed per event name.
- `type NativeModuleMethods<T> = mapped` — The methods of a native module spec T, each returning a Promise.
- `interface NativeModuleOptions` — Options for nativeModule.
- `nativePlatform(): NativePlatform` — The platform the page runs on: "ios" or "android" inside a Capacitor native shell, otherwise "web". SSR-safe ("web" when there is no window). A Capacitor custom platform (e.g. Electron) also reads "web": only the iOS and Android shells count.
- `type NativePlatform = ios | android | web` — The platform a page runs on, as denext/mobile distinguishes them.
- `interface NativeSubscription` — A subscription to a native event; remove() ends it (calling it twice is harmless).
- `nativeViewEmbedScroller(marker: number): VNode` — The element iOS embeds a "embed" slot's native view in: an overflow: scroll box filling the slot (WebKit backs it with a native scroll view) whose content is marker px taller than the box, which is how the plugin tells the slots apart.
- `type NativeViewPlacement = embed | under | over` — Where a native view is drawn relative to the WebView.
- `type NativeViewPlacementOption = NativeViewPlacement | auto` — Where a slot's native view is drawn: a NativeViewPlacement, or "auto" ("embed" on iOS, except "under" for video, whose system controls need a plain UIKit hierarchy; "over" on Android).
- `type NativeViewScrollPassthrough = vertical | horizontal | none` — Which drags that start on an "under" / "over" view scroll the page instead: "vertical" (a mostly vertical drag; taps and horizontal drags stay the view's), "horizontal", or "none" (every touch is the view's).
- `NativeViewSlot(props: NativeViewSlotProps): VNode` — A box in the page that a native view of type fills: a map, a video player, a camera preview or any view type the app registers natively (denext mobile add native-views). Give it a size. Its children are the web fallback, rendered wherever the native view is not available; overlay is DOM drawn over the native view (touches on its elements stay in the page).
- `interface NativeViewSlotHandle` — What useNativeViewSlot returns.
- `interface NativeViewSlotOptions` — Options of useNativeViewSlot.
- `interface NativeViewSlotProps` — Props of NativeViewSlot; any other prop goes to its <div>.
- `type NativeViewSlotStyle = Readonly<Record<string, string | number | undefined>>` — An inline style object, as NativeViewSlot accepts and extends it.
- `type NativeViewStatus = web | pending | native | error` — A slot's state: "web" (no native view: the children render), "pending" (the native view is being made), "native" (it is on the slot) or "error" (making it failed: the children render, and error says why).
- `type NetworkConnectionType = wifi | cellular | none | unknown` — The kind of connection a NetworkStatus reports.
- `networkStatus(): Promise<NetworkStatus>` — Whether the device is online right now, and over what.
- `interface NetworkStatus` — Whether the device is online, and over what.
- `interface NotificationAction` — An action button on a notification.
- `interface NotificationCategory` — A category: a set of action buttons notifications opt into with categoryId.
- `interface NotificationChannel` — An Android notification channel.
- `interface OfflineScreenOptions` — Options for installOfflineScreen.
- `onAppResume(cb: (awayMs: number) => void): () => void` — Call cb each time the page returns to the foreground, with how long it was away in milliseconds.
- `onBack(handler: BackHandler): () => void` — Register handler for the system back action, on top of the handlers already registered (a LIFO stack, like React Native's BackHandler). On a back action the newest handler runs first; returning true consumes it. When no handler consumes it, the default runs: history back when there is somewhere to go back to, else the app leaves the foreground (@capacitor/app's minimizeApp, exitApp where that is missing).
- `onBackProgress(cb: (event: BackProgressEvent) => void): () => void` — Call cb with each predictive-back event: the back gesture's start, its progress (0…1, with the edge it started from), then cancel or commit. Only the Android shell with denext mobile add back reports them (Android 14+ animates the gesture; earlier versions report only the commit). Elsewhere cb never runs.
- `onDeepLink(callback: (event: DeepLinkEvent) => void, options?: DeepLinkOptions): () => void` — Call callback for every link that opens the app, and (by default) navigate to it.
- `onFlexibleUpdateProgress(cb: (progress: FlexibleUpdateProgress) => void): () => void` — Android: follow a flexible update's download and install. Off Android, or without the plugin, the callback never runs.
- `onFontScaleChange(callback: (scale: number) => void): () => void` — Call callback with the new factor when the user changes the OS text size; returns a function that stops listening. Without the plugin it never fires.
- `onKeyboardChange(cb: (state: KeyboardState) => void): () => void` — Call cb each time the on-screen keyboard shows, hides or changes height.
- `onLiveActivityPushToken(callback: (event: LiveActivityPushTokenEvent) => void): () => void` — Call callback with each push token ActivityKit issues a running Live Activity: the first one of an activity started with { push: true } (or by a push-to-start push), and every rotation after it. Tokens issued before the first subscriber are kept for it. Elsewhere it is never called.
- `onLiveActivityPushToStartToken(callback: (token: LiveActivityPushToStartToken) => void): () => void` — Call callback with each push-to-start token ActivityKit issues the app (iOS 17.2 and later), including the current one: a token issued before the first subscriber is kept for it. Send each to your server, which replaces the one it had. Elsewhere it is never called.
- `onLocalNotificationReceived(callback: (notification: LocalNotification) => void): () => void` — Call callback for each local notification delivered while the app is in the foreground. Outside the shell it does nothing.
- `onLocalNotificationTapped(callback: (tap: LocalNotificationTap) => void, options?: LocalNotificationTapOptions): () => void` — Call callback when the user taps a local notification (or one of its actions), and by default navigate to its data.path (an in-app path) or data.url (under the deep-link acceptance rules), exactly as onPushTapped does for a push. A tap that cold-started the app is kept by the shell for the first listener, so subscribe early. Outside the shell it does nothing.
- `onNativeEvent<D>(name: string, event: string, handler: (data: D) => void): () => void` — Call handler with each event the native plugin name emits. Does nothing (and returns a no-op) where nativeModule would return null.
- `onOrientationChange(cb: (orientation: Orientation) => void): () => void` — Call cb with the new orientation each time the screen rotates.
- `onPushReceived(callback: (notification: PushNotification) => void): () => void` — Call callback for each notification that arrives while the app is in the foreground (one that arrives in the background shows in the tray; its tap reaches onPushTapped). Outside the native shell it does nothing.
- `onPushTapped(callback: (tap: PushTap) => void, options?: PushTapOptions): () => void` — Call callback when the user taps a notification (or one of its actions), and by default navigate to its data.path / data.url (see PushTapOptions).
- `onQuickAction(callback: (id: string) => void): () => void` — Call callback with the id of each quick action the user chooses, including the one that cold-started the app: the shell keeps that until the first listener, so subscribe early (a root layout or the app shell); only the subscribers present when it is handed over see it. Outside the native shell it does nothing.
- `onRestoredResult(handler: (result: RestoredResult) => void): () => void` — Receive the result of a picker or camera call that finished after Android killed the app (see the module docs). Register it at startup, before the first render settles: Capacitor holds the result until a listener takes it, and a listener added later still gets it.
- `onScreenReaderChange(callback: (enabled: boolean) => void): () => void` — Call callback with the new state whenever the screen reader is turned on or off; returns a function that stops listening. Without the native plugin (the web, SSR) it never fires and the returned function does nothing.
- `onShareReceived(callback: (content: SharedContent) => void): () => void` — Call callback with each share other apps send to this one, including the one that opened the app: shares wait natively until the first subscriber arrives, so subscribe early (a root layout or the app shell); only the subscribers present when a share is handed over see it. Outside the native shell, or without the plugin, it does nothing.
- `openAppSettings(): Promise<void>` — Open the app's own page in the system settings, where the user can change a permission they refused (a blocked one can only be changed there).
- `openAppStore(options?: AppStoreOptions): Promise<void>` — Open the app's store page (the App Store on iOS, Play on Android) so the user can update. Without the plugin, natively or on the web, it opens the store URL instead (the App Store when appStoreId is given, else Play when androidPackage is).
- `openAuthSession(url: string, options: AuthSessionOptions): Promise<AuthSessionResult>` — Sign in with an OAuth 2 / OpenID Connect provider in a system browser sheet, and get the callback URL the provider redirected to.
- `openExternal(url: string): Promise<void>` — Open a URL outside the app.
- `openKeyValueStore(name?: string): KeyValueStore` — Open the durable key-value store name (default "default"). Nothing is opened until the first call; every store shares one backing, and each has its own keys.
- `openPath(item: ShellItem): Promise<void>` — Open a file or folder with the OS default app (Finder / Explorer for a folder).
- `openSqlite(name: string, options?: SqliteOptions): Promise<SqliteDatabase>` — Open (creating when missing) the SQLite database name.
- `openStoreReview(options?: StoreListingOptions): Promise<void>` — Open the app's page in the App Store (on the "write a review" sheet) or Play Store, for a "Rate this app" button. Unlike requestReview it always opens something.
- `type Orientation = portrait-primary | portrait-secondary | landscape-primary | landscape-secondary` — The screen's orientation: portrait or landscape, and which way up.
- `type OrientationLock = any | natural | portrait | landscape | Orientation` — What lockOrientation locks to: a family (portrait, landscape), one exact orientation, the device's natural one, or any (every orientation the app allows).
- `type OtaApplyResult = object | object` — The outcome of applyUiUpdate when it settles. On success the webview reloads into the new UI, so the promise does not settle at all.
- `otaBooted(): Promise<void>` — Confirm to the native side that the running UI booted. Call it once after the app's first render: a UI on its trial launch that never calls it is rolled back by the native watchdog (after 15 s of foreground time by default), and on the next launch if the app died twice before confirming. Harmless on the bundled UI or a confirmed one.
- `interface OtaCheckOptions` — Options for checkForUiUpdate and prepareUiUpdate.
- `type OtaCheckResult = object | object | object | object | object` — The outcome of checkForUiUpdate. It never throws; every failure is a value.
- `type OtaErrorCode = invalid | busy | rejected | download | integrity | not_staged | signature | insecure | downgrade | native_too_old | native_mismatch` — The code of a native DenextOta refusal, carried on an error result:
- `otaInstallId(): string` — This install's stable OTA id: a random base64url string made on first use and kept in localStorage (denext:ota-install-id), so a channels server (createOtaHandler({ channels })) puts the device in the same staged-rollout bucket on every check. It identifies nothing but the install; clearing the app's data makes a new one. Where storage is unavailable it lasts for the page's lifetime.
- `interface OtaManifest` — The _denext/ota.json document: a version stamped over the sorted file list.
- `interface OtaManifestFile` — One file of an OTA UI.
- `type OtaPrepareResult = object | object | object | object | object` — The outcome of prepareUiUpdate. It never throws; every failure is a value.
- `otaReset(): Promise<void>` — Return to the UI bundled with the app: delete every downloaded version (a staged one included), forget the rejected one, and reload the webview. A no-op on the web.
- `otaSignaturePayload(manifest: Pick<OtaManifest, version | required | notes | sequence | minNative | nativeFingerprint>): Promise<Uint8Array>` — The bytes an OTA manifest signature covers, as UTF-8 with \n (0x0A) separators and no trailing newline. A manifest with a nativeFingerprint (and a sequence) uses the v3 format, one with a sequence but no fingerprint v2, one without a sequence v1:
- `otaStatus(): Promise<OtaStatus | null>` — The native side's view of the UI versions on this device, or null on the web and when the shell has no DenextOta plugin.
- `interface OtaStatus` — What the native side reports about the UI versions on this device.
- `pendingNotifications(): Promise<ScheduledLocalNotification[]>` — The local notifications still waiting to fire (none outside the shell).
- `performImmediateUpdate(): Promise<AppUpdateOutcome>` — Android: start Play's immediate update, a full-screen flow the user completes before using the app again (Play restarts the app when it finishes). Call getAppUpdateInfo first: Play refuses (info-missing) otherwise, and immediateAllowed says whether it may.
- `interface PermissionError` — A failed checkPermission / requestPermission / openAppSettings.
- `type PermissionErrorCode = unsupported | unavailable` — Why a permission call failed, as PermissionError's code reports it.
- `interface PermissionHandle` — What usePermission returns.
- `type PermissionName = camera | photos | microphone | location | location-background | notifications | contacts | calendar | biometrics` — A permission checkPermission knows.
- `type PermissionState = granted | denied | prompt | prompt-with-rationale | limited | blocked` — A permission's status, the same on every platform:
- `pickDocument(options?: PickDocumentOptions): Promise<PickedDocument | null>` — Pick a document (any file, or the types given) with the system document picker.
- `interface PickDocumentOptions` — Options for pickDocument.
- `interface PickedDirectory` — A picked file or folder as a FileDirectory: { picked: handle }. For a picked folder the path is relative to it ("" for the folder itself); for a picked file the path is "". Supported in a Deno Desktop window (the fs capability) and in browsers with the File System Access API; inside the iOS/Android shell it rejects with code "unavailable".
- `interface PickedDocument` — A file from pickDocument.
- `interface PickedFolder` — A folder pickFolder returned.
- `type PickedHandle = string` — An opaque handle to a file or folder the user picked in a dialog (pickFolder, pickDocument, saveFile). It is the only authority the filesystem and shell functions accept for a location outside the app's own folders: a result's path is for display only and is never accepted back. A handle lasts for the session (a Deno Desktop launch, or the page's lifetime in a browser); an unknown or expired one rejects with code "forbidden".
- `interface PickedImage` — A picture from pickImage: one of webPath / dataUrl, plus its format.
- `pickFolder(): Promise<PickedFolder | null>` — Let the user choose a folder.
- `pickImage(options?: PickImageOptions): Promise<PickedImage | null>` — Take a picture or pick one from the photo library.
- `interface PickImageOptions` — Options for pickImage.
- `preloadSystemIcons(names: ReadonlyArray<string | Pick<SystemIconProps, name | size | weight | scale>>): Promise<void>` — Warm the native SF Symbol cache (in the iOS shell; a no-op elsewhere), so the icons a first screen shows draw without waiting for the bridge. Call it early (before the first render).
- `prepareUiUpdate(options: OtaCheckOptions): Promise<OtaPrepareResult>` — Download and verify a newer UI WITHOUT switching to it, so the app can ask the user first.
- `interface PressEvent` — The slice of a pointer / mouse event a bound menu reads.
- `interface PrivacyScreenOptions` — How the app looks while hidden.
- `promptStoreUpdate(options?: PromptStoreUpdateOptions): Promise<PromptStoreUpdateResult>` — Take the user to a newer app binary: check the store, optionally ask (confirm), then run Play's in-app update on Android (immediate by default) or open the store page. Made for the OTA refusals that mean "this UI needs a newer binary" (native_too_old, native_mismatch): pass it as checkForUiUpdate's onNativeUpdateRequired.
- `interface PromptStoreUpdateOptions` — Options for promptStoreUpdate.
- `type PromptStoreUpdateResult = updating | store-opened | declined | up-to-date | unsupported` — What promptStoreUpdate did: "updating" (Play's in-app update started), "store-opened", "declined" (the confirm callback said no), "up-to-date" (the store has no newer build), or "unsupported".
- `PullToRefresh(props: PullToRefreshProps): VNode` — A scrolling <div> with pull-to-refresh: pull down from the top, past threshold, and let go to call onRefresh; the spinner then rests near the top and spins while refreshing is true. Set refreshing to true in onRefresh and back to false when the data arrives, as with React Native's RefreshControl (React Native mode's RefreshControl is this same gesture and spinner).
- `interface PullToRefreshProps` — Props of PullToRefresh; any other prop goes to its scrolling <div>.
- `type PullToRefreshStyle = Readonly<Record<string, string | number | undefined>>` — An inline style object, as PullToRefresh accepts and extends it.
- `interface PurchaseOffering` — An offering: the packages a paywall shows, configured in the RevenueCat dashboard.
- `interface PurchaseOfferings` — Every offering, and the one the dashboard marks current.
- `purchasePackage(pkg: PurchasePackage): Promise<PurchaseResult>` — Buy a package through the store's purchase sheet. It resolves once the store completed the purchase (and RevenueCat recorded it), and rejects with a PurchasesError: cancelled when the user closed the sheet, store for anything the store refused.
- `interface PurchasePackage` — A package: one product placed in an offering (monthly, annual, lifetime, …).
- `interface PurchaseProduct` — A store product (the fields most apps show; the SDK's full object is passed through).
- `interface PurchaseResult` — The result of a completed purchase.
- `interface PurchasesConfig` — Options for configurePurchases.
- `interface PurchasesError` — A failed purchases call.
- `type PurchasesErrorCode = cancelled | unsupported | not_configured | store` — Why a purchases call failed, as PurchasesError's code reports it.
- `interface PushNotification` — A push notification, as the shell reports it.
- `type PushPermission = granted | denied | prompt | unsupported` — Whether the app may show notifications, or "unsupported" outside the native shell.
- `interface PushRegistration` — A device's push registration: the token your server sends to, and where it is valid.
- `interface PushTap` — A tap on (or an action of) a notification.
- `interface PushTapOptions` — Options for onPushTapped and usePushTapped.
- `interface QuickAction` — One home-screen quick action.
- `readClipboard(): Promise<string>` — Read text from the clipboard: through @capacitor/clipboard inside the native shell (denext mobile add clipboard), else navigator.clipboard.readText(), which browsers gate behind a permission prompt or a user gesture. A Deno Desktop window uses the WebView's navigator.clipboard too: the desktop runtime has no clipboard capability.
- `readFile(path: string, options?: ReadFileOptions): Promise<string>` — Read a file.
- `interface ReadFileOptions` — Options for readFile.
- `readSafeAreaInsets(): SafeAreaInsets` — The device's safe-area insets in CSS px, measured once now: the same values useSafeAreaInsets reports, for code outside a component (a store, a canvas setup, a one-off layout calculation). All zero during SSR and where there is no DOM. It adds and removes a hidden element, so it forces a style calculation; to follow changes, use watchSafeAreaInsets.
- `interface RecentMediaOptions` — Options for getRecentMedia.
- `RefreshControl(props: RefreshControlProps): VNode` — Pull-to-refresh around a scroll container: pulling the container down from its top past threshold and letting go calls onRefresh; while refreshing the spinner rests at progressViewOffset. Touch only (as PullToRefresh); give mouse and keyboard users a refresh button too. Pass it to a VirtualList as refreshControl — the list renders it around its scroller with the list's class and style and passes refreshing, onRefresh and progressViewOffset from its own props.
- `interface RefreshControlProps` — Props of RefreshControl (React Native's); any other prop goes to the wrapper.
- `registerForPush(options?: RegisterForPushOptions): Promise<PushRegistration>` — Register the device for remote notifications and resolve its token, for your server to send to through APNs (iOS) or FCM (Android). denext ships no push relay: store the token on your server (with the user it belongs to) and send from there.
- `interface RegisterForPushOptions` — Options for registerForPush.
- `registerSystemIcons(icons: Readonly<Record<string, string>>): void` — Add Material Symbols SystemIcon can draw off iOS: name → the d of the symbol's path in its 960-unit grid (viewBox="0 -960 960 960", as @material-symbols/svg-* ships them). A registered name replaces a built-in one.
- `reloadWidgets(kind?: string): Promise<void>` — Ask the OS to redraw widget kind (every kind when omitted) from its stored snapshot. Outside the native shell, or without the plugin, it does nothing.
- `requestPermission(name: PermissionName): Promise<PermissionState>` — Ask for a permission when a prompt can still be shown, and report the outcome. A decided permission (granted, limited, blocked) comes back as it is, without a prompt. A refusal reads blocked on iOS (it never prompts again) and denied on Android's first refusal (a later request prompts again, after your rationale); see PermissionState.
- `requestPushPermission(): Promise<PushPermission>` — Ask for permission to show notifications, when it has not been decided yet, and report the result: "granted", "denied" (the user said no; only the system settings can change it) or "prompt" (still undecided). A decided state comes back without prompting again. Outside the native shell (or without @capacitor/push-notifications) it is "unsupported": there is no web-push fallback.
- `requestReview(): Promise<ReviewRequestResult>` — Ask the OS to show its in-app rating sheet (StoreKit's requestReview on iOS, the Play In-App Review flow on Android).
- `requestTrackingPermission(): Promise<TrackingStatus>` — Show iOS's "Allow … to track your activity" prompt (once: after an answer iOS only reports it). App Store guideline 5.1.2 requires this before any tracking, and the prompt shows NSUserTrackingUsageDescription as its reason. iOS ignores the request while the app is not active, so call it after launch settles (for example from the first screen's effect), not during startup.
- `type RestoredResult = object | object | object | object | object` — A plugin call that finished while the app was dead, as onRestoredResult delivers it:
- `restorePurchases(): Promise<CustomerInfo>` — Restore the user's earlier purchases (the "Restore purchases" button App Review expects on a paywall).
- `restoreRouteOnRelaunch(options?: RestoreRouteOptions): Promise<string | null>` — Opt in to returning to the last route after the OS killed the app in the background.
- `interface RestoreRouteOptions` — Options for restoreRouteOnRelaunch.
- `revealInFileManager(item: ShellItem): Promise<void>` — Show a file or folder selected in Finder, Explorer or the Linux file manager.
- `type ReviewRequestResult = requested | unsupported` — What requestReview did: "requested" (the system was asked to show its review sheet; whether it did is the OS's call and is never reported) or "unsupported" (not in the native shell, or no review plugin installed).
- `runBackgroundTask(name: string, details?: Record<string, unknown>): Promise<boolean>` — Run one background task now, from the page, in the runner's engine (for example after a sign-in, to warm the cache a later background run will extend). The task runs whatever its interval; its handler sees trigger: "dispatch" and details.
- `interface RunningLiveActivity` — A running Live Activity, as listLiveActivities reports it.
- `runtimePlatform(): RuntimePlatform` — The runtime the page runs in: "ios" or "android" inside a Capacitor native shell, "desktop" inside the Deno Desktop runtime, otherwise "web" (including SSR, where there is no window). The desktop case is read off globalThis.__denext.desktop, a marker the Deno Desktop runtime injects into the page before any script runs; it is a detection hint only, not a security boundary — treat it like any other client-reported value.
- `type RuntimePlatform = ios | android | desktop | web` — The runtime a page runs in, as denext/mobile distinguishes them.
- `SAFE_AREA_CSS: string` — A stylesheet fragment that defines --denext-safe-top, --denext-safe-right, --denext-safe-bottom and --denext-safe-left on :root as the device's safe-area insets (the notch, status bar, navigation bar and home indicator), 0px where there are none. Drop it into a stylesheet or a <style> tag, then pad with the variables.
- `interface SafeAreaInsets` — The device's safe-area insets in CSS px, as useSafeAreaInsets reports them.
- `interface SavedFile` — A file saveFile wrote.
- `interface SavedMedia` — What saveToLibrary saved.
- `saveFile(data: string, options?: SaveFileOptions): Promise<SavedFile | null>` — Save data to a file the user chooses.
- `interface SaveFileOptions` — Options for saveFile.
- `saveToLibrary(source: string, options?: SaveToLibraryOptions): Promise<SavedMedia>` — Save a photo (or GIF) or video to the device's photo library.
- `interface SaveToLibraryOptions` — Options for saveToLibrary.
- `scanBarcode(options?: ScanBarcodeOptions): Promise<ScannedBarcode | null>` — Scan one barcode or QR code with the camera.
- `interface ScanBarcodeOptions` — Options for scanBarcode.
- `interface ScannedBarcode` — What scanBarcode read.
- `interface ScheduledLocalNotification` — A scheduled (pending) local notification.
- `scheduleNotification(notification: LocalNotificationInput): Promise<number>` — Schedule a local notification (or show it now, without a trigger). Scheduling an id that is already pending replaces it.
- `secureStore: SecureStore` — A string key-value store for secrets.
- `interface SecureStore` — The store secureStore implements.
- `interface SecureStoreGetOptions` — Options for SecureStore.get.
- `interface SecureStoreSetOptions` — Options for SecureStore.set.
- `interface SentryCapacitorSdk` — The slice of @sentry/capacitor this uses: init(options, siblingInit).
- `interface SentrySiblingSdk` — The slice of the sibling SDK (@sentry/browser, @sentry/react, …): its init.
- `setKeyboardResizeMode(mode: KeyboardResizeMode): Promise<void>` — Change how the iOS shell resizes the app when the keyboard shows (KeyboardResizeMode), through Keyboard.setResizeMode. @capacitor/keyboard supports it on iOS only, so on Android, on the web and without the plugin this does nothing (Android resizes the WebView itself). The startup mode is plugins.Keyboard.resize in capacitor.config.
- `setNotificationCategories(categories: typeOperator): Promise<void>` — Register the app's notification categories: the action buttons a notification shows when its categoryId names one. The call **replaces** every category registered before, so pass the full set each time.
- `setPrivacyScreen(enabled: boolean, options?: PrivacyScreenOptions): Promise<boolean>` — Turn the privacy screen on or off for the whole app.
- `setQuickActions(actions: typeOperator): Promise<void>` — Replace the app's home-screen quick actions (long-press on the icon).
- `setSystemBars(options: SystemBarsOptions): Promise<void>` — Style, hide or show the system bars.
- `setWidgetData(kind: string, data: unknown, options?: SetWidgetDataOptions): Promise<void>` — Store data as the snapshot widget kind renders, and refresh that kind's widgets.
- `interface SetWidgetDataOptions` — Options for setWidgetData.
- `share(opts: ShareOptions): Promise<ShareResult>` — Open the share sheet.
- `interface SharedContent` — One share: any of a web link, text and files.
- `interface SharedFile` — A file shared to the app, copied where the app can read it.
- `interface ShareOptions` — What share shares. At least one of text or url (or title) is needed.
- `type ShareResult = shared | copied | cancelled` — How a share ended: "shared" (the sheet completed), "copied" (no share sheet, so the text was copied to the clipboard) or "cancelled" (the user dismissed it).
- `type ShellItem = string | object` — What openPath, revealInFileManager and moveToTrash act on: an absolute path inside the app's own folders (from downloadToFile), or { handle } for a file or folder the user picked (pickDocument, pickFolder and saveFile results carry one, so the result itself can be passed). A picked item's path is display-only: pass its handle.
- `showContextMenu(items: typeOperator, options?: ContextMenuOptions): Promise<string | null>` — Open a context menu and resolve the chosen item's id, or null if it was dismissed.
- `signInNative<User>(session: IdTokenSession<User>, provider: apple | google, options?: Omit<GoogleSignInOptions, nonce>): Promise<User>` — The whole native sign-in against a denext server: fetch a single-use nonce from the server, show the provider's sheet with it, and hand the id_token to session.signInWithIdToken(provider, result) (POST /auth/native/:provider), which verifies it and starts the session.
- `signInWithApple(options?: AppleSignInOptions): Promise<SocialSignInResult>` — Show the native "Sign in with Apple" sheet (iOS 13+) and resolve its id_token, the authorizationCode, and the name and email Apple sends. **Apple sends the name only on the user's first sign-in**, so pass it to the server then (signInWithIdToken does).
- `signInWithGoogle(options: GoogleSignInOptions): Promise<SocialSignInResult>` — Show Google's native account sheet (Credential Manager on Android, Google Sign-In on iOS) and resolve its id_token plus the profile's name and email.
- `interface SocialSignInError` — A failed native sign-in.
- `type SocialSignInErrorCode = cancelled | no_id_token | unsupported | failed` — Why a native sign-in failed, as SocialSignInError's code reports it.
- `interface SocialSignInResult` — What a native sign-in sheet returns: pass it to signInWithIdToken(provider, result).
- `type SqliteBackend = native | opfs | memory` — Where a database lives: the native plugin, OPFS in the browser, or memory.
- `type SqliteBindValue = string | number | boolean | null | Uint8Array | ArrayBuffer` — A value a statement binds: booleans bind as 1/0, an ArrayBuffer as a blob.
- `interface SqliteDatabase` — An open database (openSqlite).
- `interface SqliteOptions` — Options for openSqlite and deleteSqlite.
- `type SqliteParams = typeOperator | Readonly<Record<string, SqliteBindValue>>` — A statement's parameters: positional (?), or named by their placeholder, prefix included ({ $id: 1 } for $id, { ":id": 1 } for :id).
- `type SqliteRow = Record<string, SqliteValue>` — A row as an object keyed by column name.
- `interface SqliteRows` — Rows as column names plus one value array per row, in column order.
- `interface SqliteRunResult` — What a write reports.
- `type SqliteValue = string | number | null | Uint8Array` — A value SQLite stores.
- `interface SqliteWasmUrls` — The engine's two files.
- `startFlexibleUpdate(): Promise<AppUpdateOutcome>` — Android: start Play's flexible update, which downloads in the background while the app keeps running. Follow it with onFlexibleUpdateProgress, and once the status is "downloaded", call completeFlexibleUpdate (after asking the user) to install and restart. Call getAppUpdateInfo first.
- `startLiveActivity(name: string, attributes: LiveActivityValues, state: LiveActivityValues, options?: StartLiveActivityOptions): Promise<string>` — Start a Live Activity rendered by the UI denext mobile add live-activity --name <name> generated (<name>LiveActivity.swift, which reads context.attributes and context.state).
- `interface StartLiveActivityOptions` — Options for startLiveActivity.
- `stopBackgroundLocation(): Promise<void>` — Stop background location, whichever watch started it. Resolves once the plugin has stopped (at once without the plugin: stop a foreground fallback with the function watchPositionInBackground returned).
- `interface StoreListingOptions` — Where openStoreReview sends the user.
- `type SystemBar = status | navigation` — One of the system bars: the top status bar, or the navigation / gesture bar at the bottom.
- `interface SystemBarsOptions` — What setSystemBars changes; a field left out is left as it is.
- `type SystemBarsStyle = light | dark | auto` — The theme the system bars sit over: "light" (a light app, so dark icons and text), "dark" (a dark app, so light icons and text) or "auto" (the device's appearance). This is Capacitor's SystemBarsStyle; note that expo-status-bar's style names the content's color instead, the opposite way round.
- `SystemIcon(props: SystemIconProps): VNode` — The platform's icon: the SF Symbol name inside the iOS shell (natively rendered, tinted by the CSS color), the Material Symbol android (or the one mapped from name) everywhere else. SSR draws the Material Symbol; the iOS shell swaps in the SF Symbol before paint once it is cached, and hides the box for the one bridge round trip of a first render.
- `type SystemIconMode = monochrome | hierarchical | palette | multicolor` — How an SF Symbol is colored: "monochrome" (the default: the icon is a mask filled with the CSS color, so it follows the text color, dark mode and :hover), "hierarchical" (layers in opacities of color), "palette" (colors, one per layer) or "multicolor" (Apple's own colors).
- `interface SystemIconProps` — Props of SystemIcon.
- `type SystemIconWeight = ultralight | thin | light | regular | medium | semibold | bold | heavy | black` — An SF Symbol weight (UIImage.SymbolWeight).
- `type TrackingStatus = authorized | denied | restricted | not-determined | unavailable` — The ATT status:
- `unlockOrientation(): Promise<void>` — Release a lockOrientation lock (a no-op when nothing is locked, or on a browser without the API).
- `updateLiveActivity(id: string, state: LiveActivityValues): Promise<void>` — Replace a running Live Activity's state.
- `useAppResume(cb: (awayMs: number) => void): void` — Hook form of onAppResume: subscribes on mount, unsubscribes on unmount. The latest cb is always called (it is held in a ref), so passing a fresh closure each render never re-subscribes.
- `useBackHandler(handler: BackHandler, enabled?: boolean): void` — Hook form of onBack: handler is registered while the component is mounted and enabled is true, and it always sees the latest props (re-renders do not re-register it, so its place in the stack stays put). A component mounted later sits above it.
- `useBackProgress(): BackGesture | null` — Hook form of onBackProgress: the back gesture in flight (progress 0…1 and the edge it started from), or null when there is none, e.g. to drive a peek of the previous screen. Always null outside the Android shell with denext mobile add back.
- `useBackSwipe(onBack: () => void, opts?: BackSwipeOptions): (el: Element | null) => void` — Swipe right to go back. Returns a ref callback: attach it to the element that should recognize the gesture (often the page's scroll container). A touch that travels rightward at least minDistance CSS px (default 72), with horizontal travel at least ratio (default 1.4) × vertical travel, fires onBack once, as soon as it qualifies.
- `useContextMenu(items: ContextMenuItems, onSelect: (id: string) => void, options?: ContextMenuTargetOptions): (el: ContextMenuElement | null) => void` — attachContextMenu as a hook: returns a ref callback for the element. The latest items, onSelect and options are read when a menu opens, so they can change every render without rebinding.
- `useDeepLink(callback: (event: DeepLinkEvent) => void, options?: DeepLinkOptions): void` — Hook form of onDeepLink: subscribes on mount, unsubscribes on unmount. The latest callback and options are used for each link (they are held in refs), so fresh closures each render never re-subscribe.
- `useEntitlement(id: string): EntitlementState` — Whether the user has an entitlement, live: read on mount, after every purchase / restore / getCustomerInfo anywhere in the app, and each time the app returns to the foreground.
- `useFontScale(): number` — Hook form of getFontScale: the factor, read on mount and kept current. It starts at the last value read (1 before any), so the first render uses the default size.
- `useKeepAwake(active?: boolean): void` — Keep the screen from dimming and locking while the component is mounted and active is true (a video call, a recipe, a boarding pass).
- `useKeyboard(): KeyboardState` — Hook form of onKeyboardChange: the keyboard's current state, updated on every change until unmount. It reads { visible: false, height: 0 } during SSR and before mount.
- `useKeyboardInset(opts?: KeyboardInsetOptions): number` — Hook form of installKeyboardInset: installs the custom property on mount, disposes it on unmount, and returns the current keyboard height in px (0 during SSR and before mount).
- `useLocalNotificationTapped(callback: (tap: LocalNotificationTap) => void, options?: LocalNotificationTapOptions): void` — Hook form of onLocalNotificationTapped: subscribes on mount, unsubscribes on unmount, and always uses the latest callback and options.
- `useLocation(options?: UseLocationOptions): LocationState` — Hook form of watchPosition: the latest fix and error, watched while mounted and enabled. Changing accuracy or minimumIntervalMs restarts the watch.
- `interface UseLocationOptions` — Options for useLocation.
