- `useMomentumSafeScroll(options?: MomentumSafeScrollOptions): void` — Hook form of installMomentumSafeScroll: installs on mount and uninstalls when the last mounted hook unmounts. An install made by denext's runtime or directly with installMomentumSafeScroll is left in place. A change to force or settleMs re-runs the hook (it releases its share, then takes a new one); settleMs applies only when that share is the one that installs the shim, since a live install keeps its own options.
- `useNativeViewSlot(type: string, options?: NativeViewSlotOptions): NativeViewSlotHandle` — Keep a native view of type on a slot element: the hook behind NativeViewSlot. Put ref on the slot (give it a size), overlayRef on the element holding DOM drawn over the view, and, while placement is "embed", render nativeViewEmbedScroller inside it. Render your web fallback while status is "web" or "error".
- `useNetworkStatus(): NetworkStatus` — Hook form of networkStatus: the current status, updated on every change until unmount. Before mount (and during SSR) it reads { connected: true, connectionType: "unknown" }, so an offline banner never flashes on first paint.
- `useOrientation(): Orientation` — The screen's orientation, live: re-renders on every rotation. The first render reads the web API (or portrait-primary during SSR); in the native shell the plugin's answer follows.
- `usePermission(name: PermissionName, options?: UsePermissionOptions): PermissionHandle` — A permission's live status: checked on mount (or requested, with request: true), and checked again each time the app returns to the foreground, so it follows a change the user made in Settings after openAppSettings.
- `interface UsePermissionOptions` — Options for usePermission.
- `usePrivacyScreen(enabled?: boolean, options?: PrivacyScreenOptions): void` — Hide the app from the app switcher while the component is mounted and enabled is true (an account page, a banking screen). Several mounted callers share it: the privacy screen turns off once the last one unmounts or turns enabled off. On the web it does nothing.
- `usePushReceived(callback: (notification: PushNotification) => void): void` — Hook form of onPushReceived: subscribes on mount, unsubscribes on unmount, and always calls the latest callback.
- `usePushTapped(callback: (tap: PushTap) => void, options?: PushTapOptions): void` — Hook form of onPushTapped: subscribes on mount, unsubscribes on unmount, and always uses the latest callback and options.
- `useQuickAction(callback: (id: string) => void): void` — Hook form of onQuickAction: subscribes on mount, unsubscribes on unmount, and always calls the latest callback.
- `useReducedMotion(): boolean` — Whether the user asked for reduced motion (iOS Reduce Motion, Android Remove animations, the desktop setting), updated when it changes: prefers-reduced-motion, which the iOS and Android WebViews report from the OS. false during SSR. The same answer as Reanimated's useReducedMotion and React Native's AccessibilityInfo.isReduceMotionEnabled() in React Native mode.
- `useRestoredResult(handler: (result: RestoredResult) => void): void` — Hook form of onRestoredResult: listens while mounted, always calling the latest handler. Mount it high (the root layout's client provider) so it is listening when the relaunched app starts.
- `useSafeAreaInsets(): SafeAreaInsets` — The device's safe-area insets in CSS px ({ top, right, bottom, left }), kept up to date on rotation, window and visual-viewport resizes, and when Capacitor updates the insets it injects (on Android the bottom inset drops to 0 while the keyboard is up). The values are the same expressions SAFE_AREA_CSS uses, measured through a hidden fixed element, so they need viewport-fit=cover too. All zero during SSR and before mount.
- `useScreenReader(): boolean` — Hook form: whether a screen reader is on, read on mount and kept current until unmount. It is false before the first answer (and always on the web), so render the sighted layout first and let the screen-reader one replace it.
- `useShareReceived(callback: (content: SharedContent) => void): void` — Hook form of onShareReceived: subscribes on mount, unsubscribes on unmount, and always calls the latest callback.
- `useSystemBarsFollowTheme(scheme?: light | dark | null): void` — Keep the system bars' style matching the app's light / dark theme while the component is mounted: dark bars over a dark theme, light bars over a light one. With a scheme argument that is the theme; without one it follows the page, re-applied on every change: the root element's color-scheme when it names one (a theme toggle that sets it, or React Native's Appearance.setColorScheme in react-native mode), else the system's prefers-color-scheme. Only the native shell has system bars to style; elsewhere, and during SSR, it does nothing.
- `watchPosition(callback: (position: GeoPosition) => void, options?: GeoPositionOptions, onError?: (error: GeolocationError) => void): () => void` — Follow the position: callback runs with each new fix until the returned function is called. A failure (permission refused, services turned off) goes to onError; the watch keeps running where the platform keeps it (the browser does), so stop it yourself on denied.
- `watchPositionInBackground(callback: (position: GeoPosition) => void, options?: BackgroundLocationOptions, onError?: (error: GeolocationError) => void): () => void` — Follow the position in the foreground and the background: callback runs with each fix until the returned function (or stopBackgroundLocation) is called. A failure (permission refused: denied; anything else: unavailable) goes to onError.
- `watchSafeAreaInsets(onInsets: (insets: SafeAreaInsets) => void): () => void` — Follow the device's safe-area insets outside a component: calls onInsets synchronously with the current insets, then again whenever they change (rotation, window and visual-viewport resizes, Capacitor rewriting the --safe-area-inset-* it injects on <html>, and the web view applying its insets late, after the page has run), at most once per animation frame and only when they differ. It is what useSafeAreaInsets runs. During SSR (no DOM) it calls nothing and the returned stop function is a no-op.
- `writeClipboard(text: string): Promise<void>` — Write text to the clipboard: through @capacitor/clipboard inside the native shell (denext mobile add clipboard), else navigator.clipboard.writeText() (a Deno Desktop window included: the desktop runtime has no clipboard capability).
- `writeFile(path: string, data: string, options?: WriteFileOptions): Promise<void>` — Write a file, replacing it when it exists.
- `interface WriteFileOptions` — Options for writeFile.

### `denext/navigation`

- `announceRoute(message: string): void` — Announce message to screen readers now (the same text twice in a row is announced twice). Nothing happens without a document or with an empty message.
- `type Component<P> = (props: P & object) => VNode | Promise<VNode>` — A component is a function that receives props and returns a renderable node.
- `createBottomTabNavigatorFactory(core: ReactNavigationCore): (config?: unknown) => unknown` — createBottomTabNavigator for React Native mode, drawn by TabsView: visited tabs stay mounted (hidden with <Activity>), tabBarBadge / tabBarIcon / tabBarLabel / title and lazy / popToTopOnBlur / unmountOnBlur are honoured, and a press on the active tab emits tabPress (a nested stack pops to its root) then scrolls it to the top.
- `createNativeStackNavigatorFactory(core: ReactNavigationCore): (config?: unknown) => unknown` — createNativeStackNavigator for React Native mode, drawn by StackView.
- `Fragment: typeOperator` — Marker used as a VNode type to group children without a wrapping element.
- `type IosBarMaterial = glass | blur` — The iOS bar material of the platform theme: "glass" (iOS 26's Liquid Glass, approximated: a floating translucent tab bar and glass header buttons; the default) or "blur" (the iOS 7–18 translucent bars, edge to edge).
- `type Key = string | number | bigint | null | undefined` — A stable identity for a VNode among its siblings, used to keep lists reconciled.
- `type NavigationPlatform = ios | android` — The platform look a navigator takes: iOS or Android (Material).
- `type NavigationTheme = auto | platform | plain` — Which look the navigators take:
- `interface NavigationThemeProps` — The theme props every navigator takes.
- `platformThemeCss(): string` — The whole platform-theme stylesheet (exported for tests and for apps that ship it in their own CSS, e.g. to have it before the first client render).
- `interface ReactNavigationCore` — The part of @react-navigation/native (which re-exports @react-navigation/core and the routers) the factories need: import * as core from "@react-navigation/native" fits.
- `interface ReactNavigationDescriptor` — One screen's descriptor (options are the library's own screen options).
- `interface ReactNavigationObject` — The slice of the navigation object the navigators use.
- `interface ReactNavigationRoute` — A React Navigation route, as the navigators read it.
- `interface ReactNavigationState` — A navigator's state, as the navigators read it.
- `interface ScreenOptions` — Options for one screen of a stack. As a page's export const screenOptions = { … } they are plain JSON (the server reads them and ships them with the page); setOptions from useStackNavigation can also set the component-valued header* slots.
- `Sheet(props: SheetProps): VNode` — A bottom sheet. Controlled by open; the user's dismissal calls onOpenChange(false).
- `type SheetDetent = medium | large | fit | number` — A height a sheet can rest at: "medium" (half the available height), "large" (the full available height), "fit" (its content's height, up to "large"), or a number (a fraction of the available height when at most 1, else CSS px).
- `interface SheetProps` — Props of Sheet.
- `type StackAnimation = default | none | fade | fade_from_bottom | slide_from_right | slide_from_left | slide_from_bottom | simple_push | ios_from_right | ios_from_left | shared_axis_x` — How a screen enters and leaves a stack. The names follow react-native-screens' native-stack animation option:
- `StackHeader(props: StackHeaderProps): VNode` — A native-style header for a stack screen. StackLayout draws it when a screen's headerShown is true; it is exported for custom headers that want the same look.
- `interface StackHeaderProps` — Props of StackHeader.
- `StackLayout(props: StackLayoutProps): VNode` — A native-feeling stack of the routes under a layout; see the module docs.
- `interface StackLayoutProps` — Props of StackLayout. theme (default "auto": the platform theme inside the native shell), material and accentColor pick the look; see NavigationThemeProps.
- `interface StackNavigation` — The stack navigation a screen gets from useStackNavigation.
- `type StackPresentation = card | modal | formSheet | transparentModal` — How a screen is presented:
- `StackView(props: StackViewProps): VNode` — The router-independent stack view; see the module docs. StackLayout is the App Router binding most apps use.
- `type StackViewAnimate = auto | external | none` — How a change of entries animates: "auto" (the view animates it), "external" (a View Transition the owner started animates it), "none".
- `interface StackViewEntry` — One screen as the stack view draws it (bottom of the stack first).
- `interface StackViewHandle` — What StackView lets its owner do.
- `interface StackViewProps` — Props of StackView. The theme props (theme, material, accentColor) pick the platform look: see NavigationThemeProps.
- `interface TabDefinition` — One tab of a TabsLayout.
- `interface TabScope` — A tab's registry of the stacks rendered inside it.
- `TabsLayout(props: TabsLayoutProps): VNode` — A tab bar layout whose tabs keep their state; see the module docs. Render it from a "use client" component your layout uses.
- `interface TabsLayoutProps` — Props of TabsLayout. theme (default "auto": the platform theme inside the native shell), material and accentColor pick the look (see NavigationThemeProps).
- `interface TabStackHandle` — What a stack inside a tab registers, so the tab bar can pop it or scroll it to the top.
- `TabsView(props: TabsViewProps): VNode` — The router-independent tab view: panels kept with <Activity>, and the bar.
- `interface TabsViewProps` — Props of TabsView. theme, material and accentColor pick the look (see NavigationThemeProps).
- `useScreenInfo(): object | null` — The screen a component renders in, or null outside a stack. Reads id and index (0 = the stack's root screen).
- `useStackNavigation(): StackNavigation` — The stack navigation for the screen this component renders in: push, pop, popToTop, replace, canGoBack, setOptions. Outside a StackLayout the methods fall back to plain navigation and history.
- `interface VNode` — A single virtual DOM node.
- `type VNodeChild = VNode | string | number | bigint | boolean | null | undefined` — Anything that can appear as a child in JSX.
- `type VNodeChildren = VNodeChild | VNodeChild[]` — One child or an array of children, as accepted by JSX.
- `type VNodeType = string | Component<any> | FRAGMENT` — The type field of a VNode: an intrinsic tag name, a component fn, or a fragment marker.
- `interface VProps` — Props passed to a virtual node. children is normalized separately.

### `denext/virtual-masonry`

- `class MasonryLayout` — A masonry layout over count items.
- `interface MasonryPlacement` — An item's placement.
- `VirtualMasonry<T>(props: VirtualMasonryProps<T>): VNode` — A virtualized masonry (Pinterest-style) layout: items of any height in numColumns balanced columns, only those near the viewport rendered. Items are measured as they render (give getEstimatedItemSize, e.g. from an image's aspect ratio, for a steadier scrollbar); appends keep every placed item where it is; onEndReached loads the next page once per data change. Import from denext/virtual-masonry.
- `interface VirtualMasonryHandle` — The imperative handle of a VirtualMasonry.
- `interface VirtualMasonryProps<T>` — Props of VirtualMasonry.

### `denext/feature`

- `feature(name: string): boolean` — Whether the feature flag name is enabled. A feature("KEY") call with a **string literal** argument is folded to a boolean literal at build time (for a KEY listed in features) so the branch is dead-code eliminated; otherwise it reads the build-seeded flag map at runtime, defaulting to false for any unset flag.

### `denext/cli/command`

- `interface CommandContext` — The parsed invocation handed to a command's CommandSpec.run.
- `class CommandRegistry` — A registry of commands with parsing, dispatch, and help rendering.
- `interface CommandSpec` — A first-class denext CLI verb.
- `interface FlagSpec` — A declarative flag on a CommandSpec (or a global flag).
- `type FlagType = boolean | string | number` — The value kind a flag carries. A boolean flag is a bare presence switch.
- `GLOBAL_FLAGS: typeOperator` — The global flags every command accepts, as data (drives parsing + help).
- `interface GlobalFlags` — Global flags recognized on every command, parsed out before command flags.
- `type ParseOutcome = object | object | object | object` — The outcome of parsing an argv against the registry.
- `plainText(text: string): string` — text with every control character removed — C0 (\x00–\x1f), DEL and C1 (\x7f–\x9f). A verb name or summary is project content on its way to the terminal: ESC opens every ANSI/OSC sequence (cursor moves, line clears, title changes, hyperlinks), and removing the control bytes disarms them all while keeping the words.
- `interface PositionalSpec` — A declarative positional argument on a CommandSpec.
- `interface ProjectVerb` — One verb a project contributes, as CommandRegistry.formatHelp lists it.
- `suggest(input: string, candidates: typeOperator): string | undefined` — The closest name in candidates to input within a small edit-distance threshold (scaled to the input length), or undefined when nothing is close — powering "did you mean" hints for both unknown verbs and unknown flags.
- `VERB_NAME: RegExp` — A project CLI verb name: lowercase, digits and dashes, starting with a letter. The grammar denext.config.ts's commands: validation enforces (src/server/config-validate.ts), and what the help cache accepts back from disk.

### `denext/expo/apple-authentication`

- `addRevokeListener(_listener: () => void): Subscription` — Listen for the user revoking the app's access: never reported here.
- `AppleAuthenticationButton(props: AppleAuthenticationButtonProps): VNode | null` — A "Sign in with Apple" button in Apple's styles: a <button> with the Apple logo and the label for buttonType. Like Expo's, it renders nothing where Sign in with Apple cannot run (anywhere but the iOS shell); start signInAsync from onPress.
- `type AppleAuthenticationButtonProps = object` — AppleAuthenticationButton props.
- `enum AppleAuthenticationButtonStyle` — The button's look.
- `enum AppleAuthenticationButtonType` — The button's label.
- `type AppleAuthenticationCredential = object` — A signed-in user's credential.
- `enum AppleAuthenticationCredentialState` — Whether a user's Apple ID is still authorized for the app.
- `type AppleAuthenticationFullName = object` — The parts of a name.
- `type AppleAuthenticationFullNameFormatStyle = default | short | medium | long | abbreviated` — How formatFullName joins the parts.
- `enum AppleAuthenticationOperation` — The operation a request performs.
- `type AppleAuthenticationRefreshOptions = object` — Options for refreshAsync.
- `enum AppleAuthenticationScope` — What the sign-in asks for.
- `type AppleAuthenticationSignInOptions = object` — Options for signInAsync.
- `type AppleAuthenticationSignOutOptions = object` — Options for signOutAsync.
- `enum AppleAuthenticationUserDetectionStatus` — Apple's guess whether the user is a real person.
- `formatFullName(fullName: AppleAuthenticationFullName, formatStyle?: AppleAuthenticationFullNameFormatStyle): string` — A name's parts joined for display (short and abbreviated give the given name alone).
- `getCredentialStateAsync(_user: string): Promise<AppleAuthenticationCredentialState>` — A user's credential state: not provided (check it server-side with Apple's REST API).
- `isAvailableAsync(): Promise<boolean>` — Whether Sign in with Apple can run: in the iOS shell with the social-login plugin.
- `refreshAsync(_options: AppleAuthenticationRefreshOptions): Promise<AppleAuthenticationCredential>` — Refresh a credential: not provided (the plugin signs in only).
- `signInAsync(options?: AppleAuthenticationSignInOptions): Promise<AppleAuthenticationCredential>` — Show the Sign in with Apple sheet.
- `signOutAsync(_options: AppleAuthenticationSignOutOptions): Promise<AppleAuthenticationCredential>` — Sign out: not provided (Apple has no sign-out; forget the session on your side).
- `interface Subscription` — What Expo's add…Listener functions return.

### `denext/expo/application`

- `applicationId: string | null` — The bundle id (iOS) or application id (Android), or null.
- `interface ApplicationInfo` — The four constants, as applicationInfoAsync reports them.
- `applicationInfoAsync(): Promise<ApplicationInfo>` — The constants once the shell's @capacitor/app has answered (denext only; Expo's are ready synchronously). Resolves at once on the web.
- `applicationName: string | null` — The app's human-readable name (CFBundleDisplayName / the Android label), or null.
- `enum ApplicationReleaseType` — How an iOS build was distributed.
- `getAndroidId(): string` — The Android id (Settings.Secure.ANDROID_ID, per app-signing key, user and device), from @capacitor/device's getId(). Android only.
- `getInstallationTimeAsync(): Promise<Date>` — When the app was installed. No Capacitor plugin reports it.
- `getInstallReferrerAsync(): Promise<string>` — The Play install referrer. No Capacitor plugin reads it.
- `getIosApplicationReleaseTypeAsync(): Promise<ApplicationReleaseType>` — How the iOS build was distributed: SIMULATOR in a simulator (from @capacitor/device), else UNKNOWN (the provisioning profile is not readable from the web view).
- `getIosIdForVendorAsync(): Promise<string | null>` — The iOS identifierForVendor, from @capacitor/device's getId().
- `getIosPushNotificationServiceEnvironmentAsync(): Promise<PushNotificationServiceEnvironment>` — The APNs environment of the iOS build. Not readable from the web view.
- `getLastUpdateTimeAsync(): Promise<Date>` — When the app was last updated. No Capacitor plugin reports it.
- `nativeApplicationVersion: string | null` — The version string (CFBundleShortVersionString / versionName), or null.
- `nativeBuildVersion: string | null` — The build (CFBundleVersion / versionCode), or null.
- `type PushNotificationServiceEnvironment = development | production | null` — The APNs environment of an iOS build.
- `reloadApplicationInfoForTesting(): Promise<ApplicationInfo>` — Re-read the constants for the current platform: the Expo config, then the native plugins. For tests that switch between a faked shell and the web.

### `denext/expo/asset`

- `ANDROID_EMBEDDED_URL_BASE_RESOURCE: file:///android_res/` — The URL prefix of Android's embedded resources (kept for API compatibility).
- `class Asset` — A bundled file.
- `interface AssetDescriptor` — What an Asset is made from.
- `type AssetModule = string | number | object` — A module reference: a bundled file's URL, { uri }, or (unsupported) a Metro id.
- `useAssets(moduleIds: AssetModule | AssetModule[]): tuple` — Hook form of Asset.loadAsync.

### `denext/expo/audio`

- `class AudioPlayer` — An audio player over an HTMLAudioElement (created on first use).
- `interface AudioPlayerOptions` — Options for a player.
- `class AudioPlaylist` — The type of expo-audio's playlist. Playlists are not provided here (useAudioPlaylist and createAudioPlaylist are not exported): constructing this stand-in throws. Queue AudioPlayers instead.
- `type AudioPlaylistLoopMode = none | single | all` — How a playlist repeats: not at all, the current track, or the whole list.
- `enum AudioQuality` — iOS audio quality (accepted, ignored).
- `class AudioRecorder` — An audio recorder over MediaRecorder.
- `type AudioSource = string | object | null` — An audio source: a URL, { uri }, or null.
- `interface AudioStatus` — A player's status.
- `class AudioStream` — The type of expo-audio's raw PCM input stream. Streams are not provided here (useAudioStream is not exported): constructing this stand-in throws. Record with AudioRecorder, or read the microphone through Web Audio.
- `createAudioPlayer(source?: AudioSource, options?: AudioPlayerOptions): AudioPlayer` — A player not tied to a component (call remove() when done).
- `getRecordingPermissionsAsync(): Promise<PermissionResponse>` — The microphone permission (the browser's).
- `class NativeAudioModule` — The type of expo-audio's native module (what requireNativeModule("ExpoAudio") returns). There is no native module on the web: constructing this stand-in throws. Use the package's functions and AudioPlayer / AudioRecorder instead.
- `type PermissionExpiration = never | number` — When a permission expires: "never", or a timestamp.
- `interface PermissionResponse` — A permission answer, as every Expo permission API returns it.
- `enum PermissionStatus` — A permission's state, as expo-modules-core reports it.
- `interface RecorderState` — A recorder's state.
- `interface RecordingOptions` — Recording options (only web and isMeteringEnabled apply here).
- `RecordingPresets: object` — Expo's recording presets.
- `interface RecordingStatus` — A recording outcome, for the status listener.
- `requestRecordingPermissionsAsync(): Promise<PermissionResponse>` — Ask for the microphone (a getUserMedia call, stopped at once).
- `setAudioModeAsync(_mode: Record<string, unknown>): Promise<void>` — Set the audio session mode: there is no audio session on the web, so nothing changes.
- `setIsAudioActiveAsync(_active: boolean): Promise<void>` — Activate or deactivate the audio session: there is none on the web.
- `interface Subscription` — What Expo's add…Listener functions return.
- `useAudioPlayer(source?: AudioSource, options?: AudioPlayerOptions): AudioPlayer` — A player for the component's lifetime (released on unmount; a new source replaces the current one).
- `useAudioPlayerStatus(player: AudioPlayer): AudioStatus` — The player's status, updated as it plays.
- `useAudioRecorder(options: RecordingOptions, statusListener?: (status: RecordingStatus) => void): AudioRecorder` — A recorder for the component's lifetime.
- `useAudioRecorderState(recorder: AudioRecorder, interval?: number): RecorderState` — The recorder's state, polled every interval ms.

### `denext/expo/auth-session`

- `class AccessTokenRequest` — An authorization-code exchange.
- `type AccessTokenRequestConfig = TokenRequestBase & object` — An authorization-code exchange's configuration.
- `class AuthError` — An error the authorization endpoint returned.
- `type AuthErrorConfig = ResponseErrorConfig & object` — An authorization error response's parameters (plus the returned state).
- `class AuthRequest` — One authorization request: its URL, PKCE verifier and state.
- `interface AuthRequestConfig` — An authorization request's configuration.
- `type AuthRequestPromptOptions = Omit<AuthSessionOpenOptions, windowFeatures> & object` — Options for AuthRequest.promptAsync.
- `interface AuthSessionRedirectUriOptions` — Options for makeRedirectUri.
- `type AuthSessionResult = object | object` — What the prompt resolves with.
- `enum CodeChallengeMethod` — The PKCE challenge method.
- `interface DiscoveryDocument` — An OAuth / OIDC provider's endpoints.
- `dismiss(): void` — Close the open auth session, where the platform allows it.
- `exchangeCodeAsync(config: AccessTokenRequestConfig, discovery: Pick<DiscoveryDocument, tokenEndpoint>): Promise<TokenResponse>` — Exchange an authorization code for tokens (AccessTokenRequest).
- `fetchDiscoveryAsync(issuer: Issuer): Promise<DiscoveryDocument>` — Fetch issuer's OpenID configuration.
- `interface FetchRequest` — A requestAsync request.
- `fetchUserInfoAsync(config: Pick<TokenResponse, accessToken>, discovery: Pick<DiscoveryDocument, userInfoEndpoint>): Promise<Record<string, unknown>>` — Fetch the signed-in user's claims.
- `getCurrentTimeInSeconds(): number` — The current time in whole seconds.
- `getDefaultReturnUrl(urlPath?: string, options?: object): string` — The default return URL (makeRedirectUri with path).
- `getRedirectUrl(path?: string): string` — The redirect URL for path on this app (makeRedirectUri).
- `enum GrantType` — The token endpoint grant types.
- `type Issuer = string` — An issuer URL.
- `type IssuerOrDiscovery = Issuer | DiscoveryDocument` — An issuer URL, or its discovery document.
- `issuerWithWellKnownUrl(issuer: Issuer): string` — The OpenID configuration URL of issuer.
- `loadAsync(config: AuthRequestConfig, issuerOrDiscovery: IssuerOrDiscovery): Promise<AuthRequest>` — Build an AuthRequest after resolving its discovery document.
- `makeRedirectUri(options?: AuthSessionRedirectUriOptions): string` — The redirect URI for an auth request: natively native when given, else <scheme>://<path>; on the web a URL on the page's origin (localhost with preferLocalhost).
- `enum Prompt` — The OpenID Connect prompt values.
- `type PromptMethod = (options?: AuthRequestPromptOptions) => Promise<AuthSessionResult>` — What useAuthRequestResult's prompt does.
- `refreshAsync(config: RefreshTokenRequestConfig, discovery: Pick<DiscoveryDocument, tokenEndpoint>): Promise<TokenResponse>` — Refresh an access token (RefreshTokenRequest).
- `class RefreshTokenRequest` — A refresh-token grant.
- `type RefreshTokenRequestConfig = TokenRequestBase & object` — A refresh's configuration.
- `class Request<T, B>` — The base of the token-family requests: a config, a body and performAsync.
- `requestAsync<T>(requestUrl: string, fetchRequest: FetchRequest): Promise<T>` — Expo's small fetch helper: send body as a form (POST) or a query string, and read the answer as JSON (for dataType: "json" or a JSON content type) or text.
- `resolveDiscoveryAsync(issuerOrDiscovery: IssuerOrDiscovery): Promise<DiscoveryDocument>` — A discovery document: fetched for an issuer URL, returned as is otherwise.
- `class ResponseError` — An OAuth error response: an authorization redirect's or a token endpoint's.
- `type ResponseErrorConfig = Record<string, string | undefined> & object` — An OAuth error response's parameters (error, error_description, …).
- `enum ResponseType` — The OAuth response type.
- `revokeAsync(config: RevokeTokenRequestConfig, discovery: Pick<DiscoveryDocument, revocationEndpoint>): Promise<boolean>` — Revoke a token (RevokeTokenRequest).
- `class RevokeTokenRequest` — A token revocation (RFC 7009).
- `type RevokeTokenRequestConfig = Partial<TokenRequestBase> & object` — A revocation's configuration.
- `class TokenError` — An error a token endpoint returned.
- `class TokenRequest<T>` — A token-endpoint request: its grant, client and body.
- `interface TokenRequestBase` — The fields every token call sends.
- `type TokenRequestConfig = TokenRequestBase` — A token request's configuration.
- `class TokenResponse` — A set of tokens.
- `interface TokenResponseConfig` — A token endpoint response.
- `enum TokenTypeHint` — Which token a revocation names.
- `useAuthRequest(config: AuthRequestConfig, discovery: DiscoveryDocument | null): tuple` — An AuthRequest for config, its latest result, and the prompt.
- `useAuthRequestResult(request: AuthRequest | null, discovery: DiscoveryDocument | null, customOptions?: AuthRequestPromptOptions): tuple` — The latest result of request and the prompt that produces it. customOptions are the defaults of every prompt (a provider's popup size, say).
- `useAutoDiscovery(issuerOrDiscovery: IssuerOrDiscovery): DiscoveryDocument | null` — Hook form of resolveDiscoveryAsync.
- `useLoadedAuthRequest(config: AuthRequestConfig, discovery: DiscoveryDocument | null, AuthRequestInstance: (config: AuthRequestConfig) => AuthRequest): AuthRequest | null` — An AuthRequestInstance (an AuthRequest or a subclass, like a provider's) for config, once its authorization URL is built for discovery; null until then. Rebuilt when the client, redirect, response type, PKCE, state, scopes, prompt or extra parameters change.

### `denext/expo/auth-session/providers/facebook`

- `discovery: DiscoveryDocument` — Facebook's OAuth endpoints.
- `type FacebookAuthRequestConfig = AuthRequestConfig & object` — A Facebook request's configuration.

### `denext/expo/auth-session/providers/google`

- `discovery: DiscoveryDocument` — Google's OAuth / OpenID endpoints.
- `type GoogleAuthRequestConfig = AuthRequestConfig & object` — A Google request's configuration.
- `type GoogleAuthRequestHook = tuple` — What both hooks return: the loaded request, the latest response, and the prompt.
- `useAuthRequest(config?: Partial<GoogleAuthRequestConfig>, redirectUriOptions?: Partial<AuthSessionRedirectUriOptions>): GoogleAuthRequestHook` — A Google authorization request, its latest response, and the prompt. Inside the shell the code is exchanged for tokens once the prompt succeeds (see the module docs).
- `useIdTokenAuthRequest(config: Partial<GoogleAuthRequestConfig>, redirectUriOptions?: Partial<AuthSessionRedirectUriOptions>): GoogleAuthRequestHook` — A Google request for an ID token (for Firebase and your own backend): on the web it asks for id_token directly; in the shell it runs the code flow and the exchange returns it. Read it from response.params.id_token.

### `denext/expo/camera`

- `interface BarcodeBounds` — Where a code was found (not reported by denext's scanner: zeros).
- `interface BarcodePoint` — A point in view coordinates.
- `interface BarcodeScanningResult` — A scanned code.
- `interface BarcodeSettings` — The kinds a scan looks for.
- `type BarcodeType = aztec | ean13 | ean8 | qr | pdf417 | upc_e | datamatrix | code39 | code93 | itf14 | codabar | code128 | upc_a` — A barcode kind, by Expo's name.
- `Camera: object` — The permission calls and scanFromURLAsync, as Expo's Camera object groups them (expo-camera exports the permission calls only here). Camera: granted when the native scanner plugin is installed (it asks when it opens), else the browser's camera permission (a request is a getUserMedia call, stopped at once). Microphone: the browser's.
- `interface CameraCapturedPicture` — A picture takePictureAsync took.
- `type CameraMode = picture | video` — What the camera is for.
- `class CameraNativeModule` — The type of expo-camera's native module (what requireNativeModule("ExpoCamera") returns). There is no native module on the web: constructing this stand-in throws. Use Camera, CameraView and the permission hooks instead.
- `interface CameraPictureOptions` — Options for takePictureAsync.
- `interface CameraRecordingOptions` — Options for recordAsync.
- `type CameraType = front | back` — Which camera.
- `CameraView(props: CameraViewProps): VNode` — The camera view. With onBarcodeScanned it opens denext's scanner on mount and reports the first code (with a button to scan again after a cancel). Otherwise it shows a live getUserMedia preview (facing, mode, mute, active, zoom, the torch), and its ref takes pictures and records video (see CameraViewHandle).
- `interface CameraViewHandle` — The ref handle of a CameraView (what Expo's class instance offers).
- `interface CameraViewProps` — CameraView props.
- `type FlashMode = off | on | auto | screen` — How the camera flashes (applied to the torch where the track supports it).
- `type ImageType = png | jpg` — The image format of a picture.
- `type PermissionExpiration = never | number` — When a permission expires: "never", or a timestamp.
- `type PermissionHookOptions<Options> = Options & object` — Options for a permission hook (createPermissionHook).
- `interface PermissionResponse` — A permission answer, as every Expo permission API returns it.
- `enum PermissionStatus` — A permission's state, as expo-modules-core reports it.
- `interface PhotoResult` — What PictureRef.savePictureAsync resolves with.
- `class PictureRef` — A picture held in memory until saved: what takePictureAsync({ pictureRef: true }) resolves with.
- `interface SavePictureOptions` — Options for PictureRef.savePictureAsync.
- `scanFromURLAsync(url: string, barcodeTypes?: BarcodeType[]): Promise<BarcodeScanningResult[]>` — Decode the barcodes in the image at url with the browser's BarcodeDetector.
- `interface ScanningOptions` — Options for CameraView.launchScanner.
- `type ScanningResult = Omit<BarcodeScanningResult, bounds | cornerPoints>` — What CameraView.onModernBarcodeScanned listeners get.
- `interface Subscription` — What Expo's add…Listener functions return.
- `useCameraPermissions: (options?: PermissionHookOptions<object>) => tuple` — Hook form of the camera permission: [response, request, get].
- `useMicrophonePermissions: (options?: PermissionHookOptions<object>) => tuple` — Hook form of the microphone permission: [response, request, get].
- `type VideoCodec = avc1 | hvc1 | jpeg | apcn | ap4h` — A video codec, by Expo's name.

### `denext/expo/expo`

- `createPermissionHook<P, Options>(methods: object): (options?: PermissionHookOptions<Options>) => tuple` — Expo's createPermissionHook: a hook returning [response, request, get] that reads (or, with request: true, requests) the permission on mount.
- `disableErrorHandling(): void` — Turn off Expo's global error handler (there is none here): does nothing.
- `class EventEmitter<Events>` — A typed event emitter, as Expo modules use.
- `fetch(input: RequestInfo | URL, init?: RequestInit): Promise<Response>` — expo/fetch: the platform's WinterCG fetch (streaming bodies included).
- `getExpoGoProjectConfig(): null` — The Expo Go project config: none.
- `installOnUIRuntime(_uiRuntimeHolder?: object): void` — Install Expo Modules on the worklets UI runtime (there is no UI runtime here): does nothing.
- `isRunningInExpoGo(): boolean` — Whether the app runs in Expo Go: never.
- `interface Listenable` — The slice of an emitter useEvent and useEventListener use.
- `class NativeModule<Events>` — A module implemented in JS (see registerWebModule).
- `type PermissionExpiration = never | number` — When a permission expires: "never", or a timestamp.
- `type PermissionHookOptions<Options> = Options & object` — Options for a permission hook (createPermissionHook).
- `interface PermissionResponse` — A permission answer, as every Expo permission API returns it.
- `enum PermissionStatus` — A permission's state, as expo-modules-core reports it.
- `registerRootComponent<P>(component: Component<P>): void` — Mount component as the app: react-native-web's AppRegistry in React Native mode (the app key main, as Expo registers it), else denext's createRoot.
- `registerWebModule<T>(moduleImplementation: T | parenthesized, _moduleName?: string): T` — Register a module implemented in JS: a class is instantiated, an object returned as is.
- `reloadAppAsync(_reason?: string): Promise<void>` — Reload the app (the page).
- `requireNativeModule<T>(moduleName: string): T` — The native module moduleName: the Capacitor plugin of that name inside the iOS/Android shell, or the desktop extension of that name on Deno Desktop. Its functions take Expo's positional arguments and return Promises. Where neither exists (a browser, a test) it returns a stand-in whose functions throw when called, so a module that asks for it at import time still loads (Expo's web build throws at the requireNativeModule call itself).
- `requireNativeView<P>(moduleName: string, viewName?: string): Component<P>` — A native view as a component: denext/mobile's native view slot for the type nativeViewType names (the DenextNativeViews plugin, denext mobile add native-views). Its JSON props go to the native factory, a native event name calls the on<Name> prop with { nativeEvent }, style styles the slot and its children are drawn over the view. Where that view type is not registered natively (the web), the children render instead.
- `requireOptionalNativeModule<T>(moduleName: string): T | null` — The native module moduleName when this runtime has it (see requireNativeModule), else null.
- `class SharedObject<Events>` — An object shared with native code: a JS object here, released explicitly.
- `class SharedRef<Type, Events>` — A reference to a native resource (an image, a file): a JS object here.
- `interface Subscription` — What Expo's add…Listener functions return.
- `useEvent<T>(emitter: Listenable, eventName: string, initialValue?: T | null): T | null` — The latest payload of eventName on emitter.
- `useEventListener(emitter: Listenable, eventName: string, listener: (...args: never[]) => void): void` — Call listener for each eventName on emitter while mounted.

### `denext/expo/file-system`

- `copyAsync(_options: object): Promise<never>`
- `createDownloadResumable(_uri: string, _fileUri: string, _options?: Record<string, unknown>, _callback?: (progress: unknown) => void, _resumeData?: string): never`

- `class File` — A file. The instance is a path: it need not exist.

- `interface FileInfo` — What File.info reports.
- `enum FileMode` — A file-handle mode (file handles are not provided; kept for API compatibility).
- `class FileSystemEntry` — What File and Directory share: the URI, copy and move.

- `getContentUriAsync(_fileUri: string): Promise<never>`
- `getFreeDiskStorageAsync(): Promise<never>`
- `getInfoAsync(_fileUri: string, _options?: Record<string, unknown>): Promise<never>`
- `getTotalDiskCapacityAsync(): Promise<never>`
- `makeDirectoryAsync(_fileUri: string, _options?: Record<string, unknown>): Promise<never>`
- `moveAsync(_options: object): Promise<never>`
- `interface PathInfo` — What Paths.info reports.
- `class Paths` — The app's standard folders, and path helpers.
- `readAsStringAsync(_fileUri: string, _options?: Record<string, unknown>): Promise<never>`
- `readDirectoryAsync(_fileUri: string): Promise<never>`
- `interface RelocationOptions` — Options for copy and move.
- `uploadAsync(_url: string, _fileUri: string, _options?: Record<string, unknown>): Promise<never>`
- `enum UploadType` — An upload body kind (upload tasks are not provided; kept for API compatibility).
- `writeAsStringAsync(_fileUri: string, _contents: string, _options?: Record<string, unknown>): Promise<never>`

### `denext/expo/file-system/legacy`

- `bundleDirectory: string | null` — The bundled assets: the page's own origin (read-only).
- `cacheDirectory: string | null` — The app's cache folder (file:///cache/); the OS may clear it.
- `copyAsync(options: RelocatingOptions): Promise<void>` — Copy a file or folder (or anything fetch can read, such as a picker's blob: URL), replacing what is at the destination.
- `createDownloadResumable(_uri: string, _fileUri: string, _options?: DownloadOptions, _callback?: FileSystemNetworkTaskProgressCallback<DownloadProgressData>, _resumeData?: string): DownloadResumable` — Not provided (native resumable downloads): throws an error naming denext. Use downloadAsync.
- `createUploadTask(_url: string, _fileUri: string, _options?: FileSystemUploadOptions, _callback?: FileSystemNetworkTaskProgressCallback<UploadProgressData>): UploadTask` — Not provided (native upload sessions): throws an error naming denext.
- `deleteAsync(fileUri: string, options?: DeletingOptions): Promise<void>` — Delete a file, or a folder and everything in it.
- `deleteLegacyDocumentDirectoryAndroid(): Promise<void>` — Android's legacy-folder cleanup: there is no such folder here, so it resolves.
- `type DeletingOptions = object` — Options for deleteAsync.
- `documentDirectory: string | null` — The app's documents folder (file:///documents/).
- `downloadAsync(uri: string, fileUri: string, options?: DownloadOptions): Promise<FileSystemDownloadResult>` — Download a URL to a file (replacing it). As in Expo, an HTTP error status still resolves, with that status.
- `type DownloadOptions = object` — Options for downloadAsync.
- `type DownloadPauseState = object` — A paused download's saved state.
- `type DownloadProgressCallback = FileSystemNetworkTaskProgressCallback<DownloadProgressData>` — A download's progress callback.
- `type DownloadProgressData = object` — Download progress.
- `type DownloadResult = FileSystemDownloadResult`
- `class DownloadResumable` — A native resumable download. Not provided: constructing it throws an error naming denext.
- `enum EncodingType` — How File.write and the readers carry text.
- `type FileInfo = object | object` — What getInfoAsync reports.
- `type FileSystemAcceptedUploadHttpMethod = POST | PUT | PATCH` — The HTTP methods an upload may use.
- `class FileSystemCancellableNetworkTask<T>` — A native network task. Not provided: constructing a subclass throws an error naming denext.
- `type FileSystemDownloadResult = FileSystemHttpResult & object` — What downloadAsync resolves with.
- `type FileSystemHttpResult = object` — The HTTP part of a download or upload result.
- `type FileSystemNetworkTaskProgressCallback<T> = (data: T) => void` — A network task's progress callback.
- `type FileSystemRequestDirectoryPermissionsResult = object | object` — What the Storage Access Framework's permission request resolves with.
- `enum FileSystemSessionType` — The session a native network task runs in (native tasks are not provided here).
- `type FileSystemUploadOptions = parenthesized & object` — Options for uploadAsync (uploads are not provided here).
- `type FileSystemUploadResult = FileSystemHttpResult & object` — What an upload resolves with.
- `enum FileSystemUploadType` — How uploadAsync sends the file.
- `getContentUriAsync(fileUri: string): Promise<string>` — Android content URIs do not exist here: rejects with an error naming denext.
- `getFreeDiskStorageAsync(): Promise<number>` — The storage still free to this app: the origin's quota minus its usage.
- `getInfoAsync(fileUri: string, _options?: InfoOptions): Promise<FileInfo>` — Facts about a file or folder.
- `getTotalDiskCapacityAsync(): Promise<number>` — The storage available to this app in all: the origin's quota.
- `type InfoOptions = object` — Options for getInfoAsync.
- `makeDirectoryAsync(fileUri: string, options?: MakeDirectoryOptions): Promise<void>` — Create a folder.
- `type MakeDirectoryOptions = object` — Options for makeDirectoryAsync.
- `moveAsync(options: RelocatingOptions): Promise<void>` — Move a file or folder, replacing what is at the destination.
- `type ProgressEvent<T> = object` — A native progress event.
- `readAsStringAsync(fileUri: string, options?: ReadingOptions): Promise<string>` — Read a whole file as text, or as base64.
- `readDirectoryAsync(fileUri: string): Promise<string[]>` — The names of a folder's entries.
- `type ReadingOptions = object` — Options for readAsStringAsync.
- `type RelocatingOptions = object` — The source and destination of moveAsync and copyAsync.
- `StorageAccessFramework: StorageAccessFrameworkApi` — Android's Storage Access Framework. Its own calls throw or reject with an error naming denext; the aliases (readAsStringAsync, writeAsStringAsync, deleteAsync, moveAsync, copyAsync) are the functions above, for file:// URIs.
- `interface StorageAccessFrameworkApi` — The shape of StorageAccessFramework.
- `uploadAsync(url: string, fileUri: string, options?: FileSystemUploadOptions): Promise<FileSystemUploadResult>` — Upload a file with fetch: its bytes as the body (BINARY_CONTENT, the default) or as the fieldName part of a multipart form with parameters as extra fields (MULTIPART). Resolves with the response even on an HTTP error, as Expo does.
- `type UploadOptionsBinary = object` — A binary upload.
- `type UploadOptionsMultipart = object` — A multipart upload.
- `type UploadProgressData = object` — Upload progress.
- `class UploadTask` — A native upload task. Not provided: constructing it throws an error naming denext.
- `writeAsStringAsync(fileUri: string, contents: string, options?: WritingOptions): Promise<void>` — Write a whole file (creating missing parent folders), or append to it.
- `type WritingOptions = object` — Options for writeAsStringAsync.

### `denext/expo/haptics`

- `enum AndroidHaptics` — Android's haptic feedback constants for performAndroidHapticsAsync.

- `enum NotificationFeedbackType` — A notification feedback kind for notificationAsync.
- `performAndroidHapticsAsync(type: AndroidHaptics): Promise<void>` — Play an Android haptic constant. denext has no per-constant native call, so each constant plays the nearest denext kind (Confirm → success, Reject → error, No_Haptics → nothing, anything else → a selection tick), on every platform.
- `selectionAsync(): Promise<void>` — Play a selection-change tick.

- `interface ImagePrefetchOptions` — Options for Image.prefetch.

- `class ImageRef` — A loaded image: its (blob) URL, size and type. Image.Image is this class.

- `interface ImageSourceObject` — An image source object.
- `interface ImageTransition` — A fade-in: its duration (ms), timing and effect (every effect is a cross-dissolve here).
- `useImage(source: ImageSource | number, options?: ImageLoadOptions, dependencies?: unknown[]): ImageRef | null` — Load an image and return its ImageRef (null until loaded), reloading when dependencies change.

### `denext/expo/keep-awake`

- `activateKeepAwake(tag?: string): Promise<void>` — Keep the screen on until deactivateKeepAwake with the same tag.
- `activateKeepAwakeAsync(tag?: string): Promise<void>` — Keep the screen on until deactivateKeepAwake with the same tag.
- `addListener(_tagOrListener: string | KeepAwakeListener, _listener?: KeepAwakeListener): Subscription` — Listen for the platform releasing the lock. denext re-acquires the web wake lock itself when the page becomes visible again, so there is no release to report: the listener is never called.
- `deactivateKeepAwake(tag?: string): Promise<void>` — Release the hold named tag.
- `ExpoKeepAwakeTag: ExpoKeepAwakeDefaultTag` — The tag used when a call names none.

- `interface KeepAwakeOptions` — Options for useKeepAwake.
- `interface Subscription` — What Expo's add…Listener functions return.
- `useKeepAwake(tag?: string, _options?: KeepAwakeOptions): void` — Keep the screen on while the component is mounted.

### `denext/expo/linking`

- `addEventListener(_type: url, handler: URLListener): Subscription` — Call handler for each link that opens the app while it runs (the launch link comes from getInitialURL). The link is not routed: that stays the handler's job.
- `canOpenURL(url: string): Promise<boolean>` — Whether openURL would accept url.
- `clearInitialURL(): void` — Forget the launch URL (a later getLinkingURL natively reads null).
- `collectManifestSchemes(): string[]` — The URL schemes the Expo config lists (scheme: a string or an array).
- `createURL(path: string, options?: CreateURLOptions): string` — A URL that opens path in this app: <scheme>://path inside the native shell, the page's origin plus /path on the web.
- `interface CreateURLOptions` — Options for createURL.
- `interface EventType` — What a URL listener receives.
- `getInitialURL(): Promise<string | null>` — The URL that launched the app: @capacitor/app's launch URL in the native shell, the page's URL on the web.
- `getLinkingURL(): string | null` — The launch URL, synchronously: the page's URL on the web; natively, the launch URL once getInitialURL has read it, else null.
- `hasConstantsManifest(): boolean` — Whether an Expo config is available (globalThis.__DENEXT_EXPO_CONFIG__).
- `hasCustomScheme(): boolean` — Whether the Expo config names a custom scheme.
- `openSettings(): Promise<void>` — Open the app's page in the system settings, through denext/mobile's openAppSettings (denext's DenextSettings plugin, denext mobile add permissions; iOS falls back to app-settings:). Rejects on the web and on Android without the plugin.
- `openURL(url: string): Promise<true>` — Open url outside the app (denext/mobile's openExternal: the in-app browser for a web link natively, a new window on the web). Only http:, https:, mailto: and tel: are allowed.
- `parse(url: string): ParsedURL` — Split url into scheme, host, path and query.
- `interface ParsedURL` — A URL split into its parts.
- `parseInitialURLAsync(): Promise<ParsedURL>` — The parts of getInitialURL.
- `type QueryParams = Record<string, undefined | string | string[]>` — A URL's query parameters.
- `resolveScheme(options: object): string` — The scheme to build links with: options.scheme, else the Expo config's first scheme.
- `sendIntent(_action: string, _extras?: SendIntentExtras[]): Promise<void>` — Send an Android intent: not available to a web view.
- `interface SendIntentExtras` — An Android intent extra (intents are not available here).
- `interface Subscription` — What Expo's add…Listener functions return.
- `type URLListener = (event: EventType) => void` — A URL listener.
- `useLinkingURL(): string | null` — Hook form of getLinkingURL.
- `useURL(): string | null` — Hook form: the launch URL, then each link that opens the app while mounted.

### `denext/expo/local-authentication`

- `authenticateAsync(options?: LocalAuthenticationOptions): Promise<LocalAuthenticationResult>` — Ask the user to authenticate (biometrics, then the device passcode unless disableDeviceFallback). It never rejects for a refusal: the result says why.
- `enum AuthenticationType` — A biometric sensor kind.
- `type BiometricsSecurityLevel = weak | strong` — Android's biometric class (accepted, not applied here).
- `cancelAuthenticate(): Promise<void>` — Cancel a running prompt: the plugin offers no way to, so this resolves without effect.
- `getEnrolledLevelAsync(): Promise<SecurityLevel>` — How the device is secured: a biometric, a passcode only, or nothing. The plugin does not tell a weak from a strong Android biometric, so an enrolled one reads BIOMETRIC_STRONG on iOS and BIOMETRIC_WEAK on Android.
- `hasHardwareAsync(): Promise<boolean>` — Whether the device has a biometric sensor (enrolled or not).
- `isEnrolledAsync(): Promise<boolean>` — Whether a biometric is enrolled and usable.
- `type LocalAuthenticationError = not_enrolled | user_cancel | app_cancel | not_available | lockout | no_space | timeout | unable_to_process | unknown | system_cancel | user_fallback | invalid_context | passcode_not_set | authentication_failed` — Why an authentication failed.
- `type LocalAuthenticationOptions = object` — Options for authenticateAsync.
- `type LocalAuthenticationResult = object | object` — What authenticateAsync resolves.
- `enum SecurityLevel` — How the device is secured.
- `supportedAuthenticationTypesAsync(): Promise<AuthenticationType[]>` — The biometric sensor kinds the device has.

### `denext/expo/location`

- `_getCurrentWatchId(): number` — The id of the latest watch (Expo internals; a counter here).
- `enum Accuracy` — How precise a fix should be.
- `enum ActivityType` — iOS: the kind of activity (accepted, not applied here).
- `enableNetworkProviderAsync(): Promise<void>` — Android: ask to turn on the network provider (does nothing here).
- `EventEmitter: object` — Expo's native event emitter (unused here: listeners go through the watch functions).
- `geocodeAsync(address: string): Promise<LocationGeocodedLocation[]>` — Coordinates for an address, through the geocoder set with setGeocoder.
- `interface Geocoder` — A geocoding service for geocodeAsync / reverseGeocodeAsync.
- `enum GeofencingEventType` — A geofencing event (geofencing is not provided).
- `enum GeofencingRegionState` — A geofence region's state (geofencing is not provided).
- `getBackgroundPermissionsAsync(): Promise<PermissionResponse>` — The background location permission: always denied here (this shim provides no background location; denext/mobile has watchPositionInBackground).
- `getCurrentPositionAsync(options?: LocationOptions): Promise<LocationObject>` — The current position.
- `getForegroundPermissionsAsync(): Promise<LocationPermissionResponse>` — The foreground location permission.
- `getLastKnownPositionAsync(options?: LocationLastKnownOptions): Promise<LocationObject | null>` — The last known position, or null: the last fix this app got (within maxAge and requiredAccuracy), else a cached fix from the platform when it has one.
- `getProviderStatusAsync(): Promise<LocationProviderStatus>` — The provider status, as far as a WebView can tell.
- `hasServicesEnabledAsync(): Promise<boolean>` — Whether location services are on: here, whether a location source exists (a WebView cannot read the system switch; a read then fails with "unavailable").
- `installWebGeolocationPolyfill(): void` — Install Expo's navigator.geolocation polyfill: the WebView and the browser already have navigator.geolocation, so this does nothing.
- `isBackgroundLocationAvailableAsync(): Promise<boolean>` — Whether background location can run: never, here.
- `enum LocationAccuracy` — How precise a fix should be.
- `enum LocationActivityType` — iOS: the kind of activity (accepted, not applied here).
- `type LocationCallback = (location: LocationObject) => unknown` — A position callback.
- `type LocationErrorCallback = (reason: string) => void` — A watch's error callback.
- `type LocationGeocodedAddress = object` — An address a reverse geocoder returns.
- `type LocationGeocodedLocation = object` — A coordinate a geocoder returns.
- `enum LocationGeofencingEventType` — A geofencing event (geofencing is not provided).
- `enum LocationGeofencingRegionState` — A geofence region's state (geofencing is not provided).
- `type LocationLastKnownOptions = object` — Options for getLastKnownPositionAsync.
- `type LocationObject = object` — A position.
- `type LocationObjectCoords = object` — A position's coordinates.
- `type LocationOptions = object` — Options for a position read or watch.
- `type LocationPermissionResponse = PermissionResponse & object` — A location permission answer, with the platform details.
- `type LocationProviderStatus = object` — Which location providers are on.
- `type LocationSubscription = object` — What watchPositionAsync returns.
- `enum MotionActivityConfidence` — Motion activity confidence (motion activity is not provided).
- `enum MotionActivityType` — Motion activity kinds (motion activity is not provided).
- `type PermissionDetailsLocationAndroid = object` — Android permission details.
- `type PermissionDetailsLocationIOS = object` — iOS permission details.
- `type PermissionExpiration = never | number` — When a permission expires: "never", or a timestamp.
- `type PermissionHookOptions<Options> = Options & object` — Options for a permission hook (createPermissionHook).
- `interface PermissionResponse` — A permission answer, as every Expo permission API returns it.
- `enum PermissionStatus` — A permission's state, as expo-modules-core reports it.
- `requestBackgroundPermissionsAsync(): Promise<PermissionResponse>` — Ask for background location: always denied here (this shim provides no background location).
- `requestForegroundPermissionsAsync(): Promise<LocationPermissionResponse>` — Ask for the foreground location permission.
- `reverseGeocodeAsync(location: Pick<LocationGeocodedLocation, latitude | longitude>): Promise<LocationGeocodedAddress[]>` — Addresses for coordinates, through the geocoder set with setGeocoder.
- `setGeocoder(next: Geocoder | null): void` — Plug in a geocoding service (denext only; Expo's native geocoders have no WebView equivalent). Pass null to remove it.
- `useBackgroundPermissions: (options?: PermissionHookOptions<object>) => tuple` — Hook form of the background permission (always denied).
- `useForegroundPermissions: (options?: PermissionHookOptions<object>) => tuple` — Hook form of the foreground permission: [response, request, get].
- `watchPositionAsync(options: LocationOptions, callback: LocationCallback, errorHandler?: LocationErrorCallback): Promise<LocationSubscription>` — Watch the position; callback runs for each fix at least distanceInterval metres from the last one delivered.

### `denext/expo/manifest`

- `EXPO_SHIMS: Readonly<Record<string, ExpoShim>>` — Every expo-* package React Native mode aliases, by package name. A key with a subpath (expo-file-system/legacy) is a shim for that subpath of the package; its entrypoint is the package's shim name plus the subpath (denext/expo/file-system/legacy). A scoped package is shimmed per subpath only (@expo/ui/swift-ui → denext/expo/ui/swift-ui).
- `interface ExpoShim` — One shim.

- `getPermissionsAsync(_writeOnly?: boolean, _granularPermissions?: GranularPermission[]): Promise<PermissionResponse>` — The photo library permission.

- `isAvailableAsync(): Promise<boolean>` — Whether the photo library plugin is in this shell.

- `presentPermissionsPickerAsync(_mediaTypes?: parenthesized[]): Promise<void>` — Let the user change the limited selection: not available (use the system Settings).
- `class Query` — A query over the library: limit, offset, album and a MEDIA_TYPE filter (eq / within) are applied, newest first; other filters and sort orders are not (they are accepted and ignored).

- `interface ExpoPushToken` — An Expo push token, as Expo's push service issues it.
- `interface ExpoPushTokenOptions` — Options Expo's getExpoPushTokenAsync takes (accepted and not used here).
- `getAllScheduledNotificationsAsync(): Promise<NotificationRequest[]>` — The scheduled (pending) notifications, with the triggers they were scheduled with.
- `getBadgeCountAsync(): Promise<number>` — The badge count set through setBadgeCountAsync (the OS count is not readable here).
- `getDevicePushTokenAsync(): Promise<DevicePushToken>` — Register for remote notifications and resolve with the device token (APNs on iOS, FCM on Android). Rejects on the web (no web push here).
- `getExpoPushTokenAsync(_options?: ExpoPushTokenOptions): Promise<ExpoPushToken>` — Expo's push-token call. denext has no Expo push service, and wrapping the native token in Expo's shape would hand your server a token Expo's push API rejects, so this always rejects with code ERR_NOTIFICATIONS_NO_EXPO_PUSH_SERVICE: register the device token from getDevicePushTokenAsync with your own server and send through APNs / FCM with any APNs / FCM sender.
- `getLastNotificationResponse(): NotificationResponse | null` — The latest response, synchronously.
- `getLastNotificationResponseAsync(): Promise<NotificationResponse | null>` — The latest response (the cold-start tap, when there was one).
- `getNextTriggerDateAsync(trigger: SchedulableNotificationTriggerInput): Promise<number | null>` — When a trigger would next fire, computed here in the device's time zone.
- `getNotificationCategoriesAsync(): Promise<NotificationCategory[]>` — The categories registered through setNotificationCategoryAsync.
- `getNotificationChannelAsync(channelId: string): Promise<NotificationChannel | null>` — One Android notification channel.
- `getNotificationChannelsAsync(): Promise<NotificationChannel[]>` — The Android notification channels (natively on Android; none elsewhere).
- `getPermissionsAsync(): Promise<NotificationPermissionsStatus>` — Whether the app may show notifications (the plugin's state natively, the Notifications API's on the web).
- `getPresentedNotificationsAsync(): Promise<Notification[]>` — The notifications shown in the notification centre (natively).
- `enum IosAuthorizationStatus` — iOS authorization status.
- `type MaybeNotificationResponse = NotificationResponse | null | undefined` — A response, null (none), or undefined (not known yet).
- `type MonthlyTriggerInput = object` — Every month on day at hour:minute.
- `interface Notification` — A delivered notification.
- `interface NotificationAction` — A button on a notification category.
- `interface NotificationBehavior` — How a foreground notification is presented.
- `interface NotificationCategory` — A category: action buttons a notification opts into with categoryIdentifier.
- `type NotificationCategoryOptions = object` — Options for a category.
- `interface NotificationChannel` — An Android notification channel.
- `type NotificationChannelInput = Partial<Omit<NotificationChannel, id>> & object` — What setNotificationChannelAsync takes.
- `interface NotificationContent` — A notification's content.
- `type NotificationContentInput = object` — What a scheduled notification shows.
- `interface NotificationHandler` — Decides how foreground notifications are presented.
- `interface NotificationPermissionsRequest` — Which permissions to request (the iOS flags are accepted and ignored).
- `interface NotificationPermissionsStatus` — A permission answer with the platform details.
- `interface NotificationRequest` — A notification request: its id, content and trigger.
- `interface NotificationRequestInput` — A notification to schedule.
- `interface NotificationResponse` — The user's response to a notification (a tap or an action).
- `type NotificationTriggerInput = null | ChannelAwareTriggerInput | SchedulableNotificationTriggerInput` — When a notification is delivered: null for now.
- `type PermissionExpiration = never | number` — When a permission expires: "never", or a timestamp.
- `interface PermissionResponse` — A permission answer, as every Expo permission API returns it.
- `enum PermissionStatus` — A permission's state, as expo-modules-core reports it.
- `type PushTokenListener = (token: DevicePushToken) => void` — A push-token listener.

- `enum SchedulableTriggerInputTypes` — Local-notification trigger kinds, for scheduleNotificationAsync.
- `scheduleNotificationAsync(request: NotificationRequestInput): Promise<string>` — Schedule a local notification (denext mobile add local-notifications). A null trigger delivers it now; identifier defaults to a new UUID, and scheduling it again replaces it. Outside the shell a notification for now shows through the Notifications API, and a later one rejects (no scheduler).
- `setBadgeCountAsync(count: number, _options?: SetBadgeCountOptions): Promise<boolean>` — Set the app badge through the Badging API where the browser (or installed PWA) has it.
- `interface SetBadgeCountOptions` — Options for setBadgeCountAsync.
- `setNotificationCategoryAsync(identifier: string, actions: NotificationAction[], options?: NotificationCategoryOptions): Promise<NotificationCategory>` — Register (or replace) a category of action buttons. On iOS it also applies to remote pushes whose aps.category names it.

- `setNotificationHandler(next: NotificationHandler | null): void` — Set the handler foreground notifications go through. The shell's presentation is set by the Capacitor plugin's presentationOptions, so the behaviour it returns is not applied; the handler is still called, with handleSuccess / handleError.
- `interface Subscription` — What Expo's add…Listener functions return.
- `type TimeIntervalTriggerInput = object` — seconds from now; with repeats, every seconds (at least 60).
- `unregisterForNotificationsAsync(): Promise<void>` — Unregister from remote notifications (natively; nothing to do on the web).
- `useLastNotificationResponse(): MaybeNotificationResponse` — Hook form: the latest response (undefined until known, null when there is none).
- `type WeeklyTriggerInput = object` — Every week on weekday (1–7, 1 = Sunday) at hour:minute.
- `type YearlyTriggerInput = object` — Every year on month (0–11, as Expo's) / day at hour:minute.

### `denext/expo/tracking-transparency`

- `getAdvertisingId(): string | null` — The advertising id (IDFA / AAID). The plugin does not read it, so this is always null, as it is in Expo's web build and on iOS without permission.
- `getTrackingPermissionsAsync(): Promise<PermissionResponse>` — The tracking permission, without prompting.
- `isAvailable(): boolean` — Whether App Tracking Transparency can be asked for here: the iOS shell with the AppTrackingTransparency plugin installed (Expo's call is synchronous, so this checks the plugin's presence rather than asking it).
- `type PermissionExpiration = never | number` — When a permission expires: "never", or a timestamp.
- `type PermissionHookOptions<Options> = Options & object` — Options for a permission hook (createPermissionHook).
- `interface PermissionResponse` — A permission answer, as every Expo permission API returns it.
- `enum PermissionStatus` — A permission's state, as expo-modules-core reports it.
- `requestTrackingPermissionsAsync(): Promise<PermissionResponse>` — Ask for the tracking permission: the system ATT prompt in the iOS shell (shown once per install; later calls report the stored answer).
- `useTrackingPermissions: (options?: PermissionHookOptions<object>) => tuple` — Hook form of the tracking permission: [response, request, get].

- `interface ButtonType` — A dialog button's label and colour (Android).
- `DateTimePicker(props: DateTimePickerProps): VNode` — A date / time picker: an inline input, or (in the Android shell) a dialog opened on mount.

- `interface DateTimePickerEvent` — The event onChange receives.
- `type DateTimePickerMode = date | time | datetime | countdown` — The picker's mode.
- `interface DateTimePickerProps` — DateTimePicker props (the iOS and Android props together, plus any view prop).
- `default`
- `type EvtTypes = set | neutralButtonPressed | dismissed` — What happened: a date was picked, the dialog was dismissed, or the neutral button pressed.

### `denext/expo/updates`

- `channel: string | null` — The release channel (not used here): null.
- `checkAutomatically: UpdatesCheckAutomaticallyValue | null` — When updates are checked: NEVER (the app asks).
- `checkForUpdateAsync(): Promise<UpdateCheckResult>` — Check the update server, and stage a newer UI when there is one (it is downloaded and verified now, so fetchUpdateAsync has nothing left to do).
- `clearLogEntriesAsync(): Promise<void>` — Clear the update log: nothing to clear.
- `createdAt: Date | null` — When the running update was created: null.
- `emergencyLaunchReason: string | null` — Why this is an emergency launch: null.
- `class ExpoUpdatesModule` — The type of expo-updates' native module (what requireNativeModule("ExpoUpdates") returns). There is no native module on the web: constructing this stand-in throws. Use the package's functions (checkForUpdateAsync, fetchUpdateAsync, reloadAsync) and constants instead.
- `fetchUpdateAsync(): Promise<UpdateFetchResult>` — Download the update: the check already staged it, so this reports it.
- `getExtraParamsAsync(): Promise<Record<string, string>>` — The extra request parameters (not used here): empty.
- `isEmbeddedLaunch: true` — Whether the embedded bundle is running (not tracked here): true.
- `isEmergencyLaunch: false` — Whether this is an emergency launch: false.
- `isEnabled: boolean` — Whether updates are enabled (in the native shell with updates.url set).
- `isUsingEmbeddedAssets: true` — Whether embedded assets are used: true.
- `launchDuration: number | null` — How long the launch took: null.
- `localAssets: Record<string, string>` — The local asset map: empty.
- `manifest: Partial<Manifest>` — The running manifest (not tracked here): empty.
- `interface Manifest` — An update's manifest, as far as denext knows it.
- `readLogEntriesAsync(_maxAge?: number): Promise<UpdatesLogEntry[]>` — The update log: empty (denext's OTA client reports through its results).
- `reloadAsync(_options?: object): Promise<void>` — Switch to the staged update (the page reloads into it), or reload the page when none is staged.
- `runtimeVersion: string | null` — The runtime version (not used here): null.
- `setExtraParamAsync(_key: string, _value: string | null | undefined): Promise<void>` — Set an extra request parameter: not used here (does nothing).
- `type UpdateCheckResult = object | object` — What checkForUpdateAsync resolves with.
- `enum UpdateCheckResultNotAvailableReason` — Why no update is available.
- `type UpdateFetchResult = object | object` — What fetchUpdateAsync resolves with.
- `updateId: string | null` — The running update's id (not tracked here): null.
- `enum UpdatesCheckAutomaticallyValue` — When updates are checked automatically.
- `interface UpdatesLogEntry` — A log entry (there are none here).
- `useUpdates(): UseUpdatesReturnType` — Hook form of the update state: a static snapshot here (no state machine is exposed).
- `interface UseUpdatesReturnType` — What useUpdates returns.

### `denext/expo/video`

- `clearVideoCacheAsync(): Promise<void>` — Clear the video cache (the browser owns it): nothing to do.
- `createVideoPlayer(source: VideoSource, _playerBuilderOptions?: PlayerBuilderOptions): VideoPlayer` — A player not tied to a component (call release() when done).
- `getCurrentVideoCacheSize(): number` — The video cache size (the browser owns it): 0.
- `isPictureInPictureSupported(): boolean` — Whether Picture in Picture is supported: not through this shim.
- `interface PlayerBuilderOptions` — Android player-builder options (seek increments), applied before the native player is built. Accepted and ignored here: the browser's controls set their own increments.
- `setVideoCacheSizeAsync(_sizeBytes: number): Promise<void>` — Set the video cache size (the browser owns it): nothing to do.
- `interface Subscription` — What Expo's add…Listener functions return.
- `useVideoPlayer(source: VideoSource, setup?: (player: VideoPlayer) => void, _playerBuilderOptions?: PlayerBuilderOptions): VideoPlayer` — A player for the component's lifetime.
- `class VideoPlayer` — A video player: an HTMLVideoElement, or the native video view it is shown in.
- `interface VideoPlayerEvents` — The events a player emits.
- `type VideoPlayerStatus = idle | loading | readyToPlay | error` — The player's load state.
- `type VideoSource = string | object | null` — A video source: a URL, { uri }, or null.
- `VideoView(props: VideoViewProps): VNode` — Shows a player's video: in the native video view where it is registered, else in the player's <video>.
- `interface VideoViewProps` — VideoView props.

### `denext/expo/web-browser`

- `type AuthSessionOpenOptions = WebBrowserOpenOptions & object` — Options for openAuthSessionAsync.
- `coolDownAsync(_browserPackage?: string): Promise<ServiceActionResult>` — Release a warmed-up Custom Tabs browser (Android): nothing to do here.
- `dismissAuthSession(): void` — Dismiss the auth session: not controllable here (it ends on redirect or cancel).
- `dismissBrowser(): Promise<object>` — Dismiss the in-app browser: not controllable here.
- `getCustomTabsSupportingBrowsersAsync(): Promise<WebBrowserCustomTabsResults>` — The browsers supporting Custom Tabs (Android): none are listed here.
- `maybeCompleteAuthSession(_options?: WebBrowserCompleteAuthSessionOptions): WebBrowserCompleteAuthSessionResult` — On a web redirect page opened by openAuthSessionAsync: hand this page's URL back to the opener and close the popup.
- `mayInitWithUrlAsync(_url: string, _browserPackage?: string): Promise<ServiceActionResult>` — Pre-load a URL in a Custom Tabs browser (Android): nothing to do here.
- `openAuthSessionAsync(url: string, redirectUrl?: string | null, options?: AuthSessionOpenOptions): Promise<WebBrowserAuthSessionResult>` — Sign in through an auth session: open url and resolve with the URL the provider redirects to.
- `openBrowserAsync(url: string, _options?: WebBrowserOpenOptions): Promise<WebBrowserResult>` — Open url in the in-app browser (native) or a new window (web).
- `interface ServiceActionResult` — What the Custom Tabs warm-up calls resolve with.
- `warmUpAsync(_browserPackage?: string): Promise<ServiceActionResult>` — Warm up a Custom Tabs browser (Android): nothing to do here.
- `type WebBrowserAuthSessionResult = WebBrowserRedirectResult | WebBrowserResult` — What openAuthSessionAsync resolves with.
- `interface WebBrowserCompleteAuthSessionOptions` — Options for maybeCompleteAuthSession.
- `interface WebBrowserCompleteAuthSessionResult` — What maybeCompleteAuthSession returns.
- `interface WebBrowserCustomTabsResults` — What getCustomTabsSupportingBrowsersAsync resolves with.
- `interface WebBrowserOpenOptions` — Options for openBrowserAsync (all accepted, none needed here).
- `enum WebBrowserPresentationStyle` — The iOS presentation style (ignored here).
- `interface WebBrowserRedirectResult` — A successful auth session: the redirect URL.
- `interface WebBrowserResult` — A plain session result.
- `enum WebBrowserResultType` — How a browser session ended.
- `type WebBrowserWindowFeatures = Record<string, number | boolean | string>` — Window features for the web popup (ignored here).

### `denext/expo/widgets`

- `addPushToStartTokenListener(listener: (event: PushToStartTokenEvent) => void): Subscription` — Listen for the push-to-start tokens ActivityKit issues the app (iOS 17.2+), the current one included.
- `addUserInteractionListener(_listener: (event: UserInteractionEvent) => void): Subscription` — Listen for widget taps: never called here (the generated widgets open the app).
- `after(date: Date): object` — A dismissal policy: remove the ended activity at date (iOS caps it at four hours).
- `createLiveActivity<T>(name: string, liveActivity: LiveActivityComponent<T>): LiveActivityFactory<T>` — Declare a Live Activity name.
- `createWidget<PropsType, ConfigurationType>(name: string, widget: (props: PropsType, context: WidgetEnvironment<ConfigurationType>) => unknown): Widget<PropsType, ConfigurationType>` — Declare a widget.
- `class LiveActivity<T>` — A running Live Activity.
- `type LiveActivityComponent<T> = (props: T, environment: Record<string, unknown>) => unknown` — A Live Activity layout function (never rendered here).
- `type LiveActivityDismissalPolicy = default | immediate | object` — How an ended Live Activity is dismissed: at once, the system's default, or at a time.
- `class LiveActivityFactory<T>` — Starts and lists the Live Activities of one name.
- `interface PushTokenEvent` — A Live Activity push token event.
- `interface PushToStartTokenEvent` — A push-to-start token event (iOS 17.2+).
- `interface Subscription` — What Expo's add…Listener functions return.
- `interface UserInteractionEvent` — A widget interaction event (never emitted here).
- `class Widget<PropsType, _ConfigurationType>` — A home-screen widget: its updates store the JSON snapshot the native widget renders.
- `type WidgetEnvironment<T> = object` — What a widget layout receives besides its props (never rendered here).
- `widgetsDirectory: literal` — The shared widgets folder: none here (widgets read the JSON snapshot, not files).
- `interface WidgetTimelineEntry<T>` — A widget's timeline entry.
